Warren County by the numbers

Who sends and collects a Warren County tax bill?

Warren County divides the job three ways, and all three offices answer calls on weekdays. One office values the house, a second sends the bill and takes payment, and a third picks up any balance left on April 15.

  • PVA: 429 E. 10th Avenue, Bowling Green, KY 42101, phone (270) 843-3268 per the county's department list, open 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Sheriff: (270) 842-1633, with a tax inquiry page for looking up and paying a bill. Its business office keeps the same 8:00 to 4:30 hours.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, phone (270) 842-9416. The clerk's own site sends property tax and valuation questions to the PVA.

The sheriff's page grounds the office's collector role in KRS 134.140 and 160.500, and says it passes the money on to each state, county, school and district authority.

What does the sheriff's 2026 payment schedule look like?

The sheriff's site laid out the 2026 dates and told owners to expect a bill in the first week of October. Each stage tracks the state calendar in KRS 134.015.

  • October 1 to November 1, 2026: 2 percent off.
  • November 2 to December 31, 2026: the amount on the bill.
  • January 2027: 5 percent more.
  • February 1 to April 15, 2027: a 21 percent charge that bundles the 10 percent penalty with the sheriff's fee.

The 2026 discount window closed November 1, 2026. Paying online carries a cost: $1.50 for a card payment of $60.00 or less, 2.49 percent above that, and $1.50 per ACH or e-check payment. American Express is refused. The site refreshes after 7:00 pm on business days, so a Friday payment may not appear until Monday night. On a large bill, an ACH payment avoids the percentage.

Why do two Warren County neighbors pay different rates?

Warren County has two public school districts. Warren County Public Schools serves the county and the outlying parts of Bowling Green, and Bowling Green Independent Schools serves most of the city proper. The clerk's 2025 rate sheet shows how big that choice is: a city school levy of 84.80 cents against 52.20 cents for the county district.

Warren County 2025 real estate levies, cents per $100 of assessed value (County Clerk rate sheet)
LevyCents
State10.60
County general fund14.00
Library3.70
Public health2.90
Extension and conservation0.85
City20.30
School, county district52.20
School, city district84.80

The county levies add to 21.45 cents. Adding the pieces yields three combined rates: 84.25 for land outside any city, 104.55 for city land in the county school district, and 137.15 for city land in the city school district. Ask the sheriff which combination your address pays.

What would the median Warren County house owe?

QuickFacts lists $258,000 as the midpoint home value. Assuming an assessment at that figure, the three combined rates produce annual bills of roughly $2,173.65 in the unincorporated county, $2,697.39 in a city with county schools, and $3,538.47 in a city with its own school district. The gap of more than $1,300 between the first and the last is something a buyer will notice.

Assessments and sale prices rarely match, so treat these figures as a way to compare districts. A homeowner who qualifies for the $49,100 exemption pays on $208,900 instead, which saves about $413.67 a year at the 84.25 rate.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Warren County?

Claims go to the PVA from owners who are 65 and over or who count as totally disabled. The deduction is $49,100 for each of 2025 and 2026, and a birth certificate, license or passport backs up the age claim. The QuickFacts count of residents who are 65 or older is 14.2 percent.

A disability claim comes up for yearly renewal. Two groups never renew: service disabled veterans, and owners whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rated permanently and totally disabled.

How do I contest a Warren County value?

Book a conference with the PVA at the number in the county directory, (270) 843-3268, since state rules make it the first step. Viewing of the roll lasts thirteen days, beginning the first Monday in May. A taxpayer who has met with the PVA then files at the County Clerk before the day after inspection ends.

  • Photos, insurance records, building costs and sales listings are the evidence the local board expects.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you must be a professional such as an attorney, accountant, appraiser or broker, and must carry written authority.
  • Hearings start 25 to 35 days after viewing ends and run no more than five days.

Written reasons accompany any decision to raise or lower a value.

What does the Warren County Clerk do with bills unpaid on April 15?

At the close of that day, the sheriff sends over every open bill as a certificate of delinquency carrying a lien. The clerk keeps accepting payment right up to the annual sale and publishes a PDF list of current delinquent parcels. For 2026 the clerk scheduled the sale at 9:00 am on August 26 in Suite 100 at 429 E 10th Ave, with buyer registration due August 17. Both dates have passed.

After the transfer, costs layer on quickly. The meter runs at 1 percent monthly. The clerk's commission is 10 percent of tax, penalty and interest, and the county attorney adds 20 percent unless the bill is paid within five business days. A $10 lien recording and release fee also applies. Because the lien clings to the land for up to eleven years, sellers should pay it off at closing and get a release from the clerk.

What else should a Warren County seller know about the county?

Warren was carved from Logan County in 1796 and is Kentucky's fifth most populous county, with Bowling Green as its seat. Barren River runs through the city, with the Green River marking the north edge. Interstate 65 and the Natcher Parkway (renamed I-165 in 2019), turned a farming county into a manufacturing one in the 1960s and 1970s. Cities besides Bowling Green are Oakland, Plum Springs, Smiths Grove and Woodburn. Visitors know it for Western Kentucky University, Beech Bend Park, the Corvette assembly plant and the National Corvette Museum.

Census QuickFacts shows the growth: 149,375 people in mid 2025, with 1,453 building permits issued during the year. Rent at the median is $1,002 a month, and 55.6 percent of homes are lived in by owners. Among adults, 32.3 percent have a bachelor's degree, and 10.4 percent of residents were born outside the country.

Permits matter. The county's Division for Building Services, at 1141 State Street, covers everywhere except Bowling Green and Oakland, charges $0.15 per square foot with a $45 minimum, and sets a fine of at least $500 for work begun without a permit. Sheds from 120 square feet and all pools need one. Phone (270) 843-5360 to ask about a past project before you list.

More questions about Warren County, KY Property Tax Guide

Which office takes payment for Warren County property tax?

The Warren County Sheriff's Office takes it, at (270) 842-1633. Use the tax inquiry page on its website to look up and pay a bill.

Did the 2026 Warren County discount end?

Yes. The window was October 1 to November 1, 2026. After that the face amount stands until December 31, 2026, and January 2027 adds 5 percent.

Why is the Warren County school tax higher in some places?

The city school district levy is 84.80 cents per $100, against 52.20 cents for the county district, according to the clerk's 2025 rate sheet. Parcels inside the city's own district pay the higher one.

Does Warren County charge extra to pay by card?

Yes. Card payments run $1.50 up to $60.00 and 2.49 percent over that. ACH and e-check payments cost $1.50, and American Express is not accepted.

What is the population of Warren County?

The Census estimate is 149,375 for July 2025. That is 11.0 percent above the April 2020 base of 134,563, and the clerk's own website calls the county the fastest growing in Kentucky.

  • County tax bill payable online at fcsoky.net by credit/debit card; may take 24 hours to post; office 974 River Bend Road, Frankfort, (502) 875-8740 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Tax rate

Selling in Franklin County?

Franklin County by the numbers

Why can a Frankfort house have two tax bills?

Because the City of Frankfort taxes inside its limits on top of the county. Everyone in Franklin County gets a county bill from the Franklin County Sheriff, and a house in Frankfort also gets a city bill from the Finance Office, which collects for Frankfort Independent Schools too.

The Franklin County PVA sets the values for both bills. The county lists the office at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, with a fax at (502) 226-5495 and a phone at (502) 875-8780, open weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30. The sheriff moved to the Public Safety Complex at 974 River Bend Road and answers at (502) 875-8740. The sheriff's website offers a tax bill search with card payment, and the front door has a secure drop box under camera watch.

Frankfort says it works from the PVA's figure, which is 100 percent of fair market value as of each January 1. Questions about a value, an exemption or a mailing address belong with the PVA, not the city.

How do the county and Frankfort calendars differ?

The city does not copy the state schedule. County bills follow KRS 134.015, while Frankfort publishes its own dates, so a deadline that works for one bill can already be past for the other.

Sheriff bill and City of Frankfort bill side by side (sources: KRS 134.015, City of Frankfort Finance Office)
FeatureCounty billCity of Frankfort bill
Early-payment credit2 percent off when paid in full by November 12 percent off for money received before November 30
Face amount windowNovember 2 through December 31Bills available by November 1, due December 31
After the deadline5 percent in January, then 10 percent10 percent plus interest
Where to paySheriff's office or onlineFinance Office at (502) 875-8500, or the city's online portal

The city also reminds owners with escrow accounts to hand the bill to the servicer, since the lender cannot pay what it never received. City commissioners vote the city rate each year on the finance director's advice, and Frankfort Independent Schools sets the old city school rate.

What kind of county is Franklin County for a seller?

Franklin County is the seat of state government, and it is more urban than most of Kentucky. It was carved out in 1795 from Woodford, Mercer and Shelby counties, and the lines of Kentucky's three original counties once met inside what is now Franklin County. The land area is 208 square miles, and six counties touch it: Owen, Scott, Woodford, Anderson, Shelby and Henry.

Interstate 64 serves the county, along with US 60, US 127, US 421, US 460 and KY 676, and Frankfort Transit runs buses. Two school systems share the area. Franklin County Public Schools covers nearly all of it, including most of Frankfort, while Frankfort Independent Schools covers downtown, South Frankfort around the Capitol, and Bellepoint. Kentucky State University is here too. Recreation includes Josephine Sculpture Park, Cove Spring Park and the wooded trails on Fort Hill, where Union troops dug earthworks before an 1864 skirmish.

Growth has been steady rather than fast. The population was 5,078 in 1800, reached 49,285 in 2010 and stood at 51,541 in 2020. The 2025 estimate of 52,649 is 2.1 percent above the 2020 base.

What do Franklin County's economy and housing numbers show?

  • Typical house value, 2020 to 2024 survey: $216,600, roughly double the Floyd County figure.
  • Owners live in 64.5 percent of homes, which leaves a large rental share.
  • Housing units: 24,404 in 2025. Households: 22,718, averaging 2.20 people.
  • Median gross rent: $967. Median household income: $65,298, with 12.3 percent below the poverty line.
  • Permits for new homes in 2025: 96.
  • Commute: 20.0 minutes on average, and 62.2 percent of adults are in the labor force.
  • Education: 92.8 percent finished high school and 31.9 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more.

State employment shows up in the data. Employer businesses numbered 1,278 in 2023 with 16,897 jobs and a payroll near $869 million, and retail sales topped $1 billion in 2022. About 73 percent of the population lived in an urban area in 2020, so sellers in Frankfort face a deeper buyer pool than most Kentucky counties can offer, and a bill that is larger in dollars.

Health care brought in about $397 million in 2022, and the county counts 3,768 businesses with no employees besides the owner. Vacancy was low when the 2020 census was taken: 9.0 percent of the county's 24,000 housing units stood empty, compared with 13.8 percent in Floyd County. A seller carrying a tax balance should collect payoff figures from both billing offices before picking a closing date.

How does an owner appeal a Franklin County assessment?

Meet the PVA first, because the state will not take an appeal from an owner who skipped the conference. The roll is posted for 13 days beginning in the first week of May, and the PVA has to advertise that period in the county's largest newspaper.

Next, file at the county clerk's office by the end of the following business day. A local board of assessment appeals then hears cases roughly four or five weeks later. It listens only to evidence offered with you and the PVA both present, so bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal, repair estimates or insurance records. You may audio-record the hearing, and the board owes you a written explanation of any change. If bills have already printed when the board raises a value, a supplemental bill makes up the gap.

Does Franklin County offer a homestead exemption?

It does for seniors and totally disabled owners. The state exemption is $49,100 in 2025 and 2026, deducted from assessed value before tax is calculated. A house worth the county median of $216,600 would be taxed on $167,500.

File with the Franklin County PVA. Ask that office how the January 1 ownership date applies if you buy or sell partway through a year, and tell it about any sale so the exemption comes off the old address.

What happens to unpaid Franklin County tax when I sell?

It follows the parcel to the closing table. KRS 134.015 treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien survives a change of ownership.

Open bills pass from the sheriff to the county clerk on April 15. From then on 1 percent interest accrues every month, the clerk takes a 10 percent commission, and a county attorney commission of 20 percent applies after the first notice goes out.

  • Ask the sheriff for a payoff at (502) 875-8740, and the city Finance Office at (502) 875-8500 if the house is in Frankfort.
  • Have the title company pay both bills from your proceeds so the policy issues clean.
  • A buyer that purchases as-is and closes quickly can take over a house with arrears and repairs without a listing period.

More questions about Franklin County, KY Property Tax Guide

Do Frankfort homeowners pay the city and the county?

Yes. They receive a county bill collected by the sheriff and a city bill collected by the Finance Office, which also collects for Frankfort Independent Schools.

Where is the Franklin County sheriff's tax office?

It is at 974 River Bend Road, Frankfort, KY 40601, and the phone is (502) 875-8740. Bills can also be searched and paid on the sheriff's website.

Where is the Franklin County PVA?

It is at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, KY 40601. The phone is (502) 875-8780, and the county lists weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30.

How big is the Franklin County homestead exemption?

It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners apply through the PVA, and the amount is subtracted from the assessed value.

How soon after April 15 can Franklin County hold a tax sale?

The sale must fall between 90 and 135 days after the sheriff transfers the bills to the clerk, and the county attorney mails notices beforehand.

Hardin County by the numbers

What sets Hardin County, Kentucky apart before a seller opens the tax bill?

Hardin County had 113,482 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, up 2.5 percent from the 2020 count, and Elizabethtown is both the seat and the biggest city. The county was formed in 1792 out of Nelson County. It touches nine other counties, which is more than any other Kentucky county, and fires took the courthouse records in 1864 and again in 1932 before the present courthouse went up in 1934.

Fort Knox dominates the local economy, and its housing sits inside Hardin County. Besides Elizabethtown, the county has the cities of Radcliff, Vine Grove, Sonora, Upton and West Point, plus Muldraugh, which lies mostly in Meade County. Hardin County Schools covers most of the county, and Elizabethtown Independent Schools serves most of the city of Elizabethtown, which matters because each district sets its own rate.

With 51,149 housing units, 432 building permits issued in 2025 and 62.6 percent of homes occupied by their owners, the market is deep enough that a conference with the assessor can lean on recent sales near your street.

Which Hardin County offices bill, assess and collect property tax?

Everything runs through the government building on North Provident Way in Elizabethtown.

  • Sheriff's Office, tax department: Suite 101, 150 North Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701. Phone 270-765-5133 and pick option 1.
  • PVA (the assessor): 270-765-2129. Its website has a parcel search, a tax estimator and an exemption page.
  • County Clerk: Suite 103 in the same building, 270-765-2171, open weekdays from 7:45 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon The clerk quotes the payoff on a delinquent prior year bill.
  • Planning and Development Commission: Suite 225, 270-769-5479, open weekdays from 8 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon for building permits outside city limits.

Two cities bill part of the tax themselves. A tax district code of 03 on your bill means the City of Radcliff (270-351-4714), and 06 means the City of Vine Grove (270-877-2422).

What is the Hardin County bill schedule for fall 2026?

The sheriff posted dates for bills due beginning November 1, 2026, which cover the assessment as of January 1, 2026. The discount period is longer than the date written into KRS 134.015.

  • Discount: November 1 through November 30, 2026.
  • Face amount: December 1 through December 31, 2026.
  • 5 percent penalty: January 1 through January 31, 2027.
  • 21 percent penalty: February 1 through April 15, 2027.

A current year bill has to be paid whole. A single payment can cover several bills when copies are attached, and a stamped, self addressed envelope brings back a receipt. Paying by card, online or at the counter, adds 2.49 percent. A taxpayer with no bill by early November can call and a duplicate goes out, or print one from the sheriff's tax bill search.

What are the 2026 real estate tax rates in Hardin County?

Rates are quoted in cents per $100 of assessed value, and the school district decides which row fits your house.

Hardin County 2026 real estate rates in cents per $100 of value, as posted by the Hardin County PVA
Tax districtStateSchoolCountyTotal
Hardin County School10.3065.2010.7090.35
Elizabethtown Independent School10.3087.3010.70112.45

The totals also include small extension, health and soil lines. Separate city rates for 2026 are Radcliff 12.9 on real estate, Vine Grove 16.3, Sonora 20.0, Upton 25.0 and West Point 26.8. Commercial and telecommunication property in the Industrial Taxing District (District 00) carries an extra ten cents under a 2023 ordinance. Timberland Fire Protection charges 2 cents per acre.

As a rough illustration, the Census median owner occupied value of $225,800 at 90.35 cents works out to about $2,040 a year before exemptions, city tax, fire fees or 911 fees. In the Elizabethtown Independent district the same value runs to about $2,539.

Can I contest my Hardin County assessed value?

The PVA publishes the inspection dates in the News-Enterprise each year and prints them on assessment notices. The window opens the first Monday in May and stays open thirteen days. Hold your conference with the PVA before or during that time.

When the conference settles things, you are finished. When it does not, hand the appeal form to the County Clerk, who sets a hearing before the county board. A further appeal goes to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Collect sale prices from your own neighborhood first. In the Elizabethtown Independent district each dollar of assessed value carries a higher rate, so a successful appeal saves more there than in the county school district.

What does the homestead exemption save a Hardin County owner?

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners totally disabled, who live in the house can apply at the PVA. The PVA's rate page lists the homestead and disability amount at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, after $46,350 for 2023 and 2024.

That figure comes off the assessed value, so the saving depends on your rate. At 90.35 cents, $49,100 is worth about $444 a year. Questions go to the PVA at 270-765-2129. A buyer has to apply separately after closing, because the exemption belongs to the owner.

Who pays the Hardin County tax bill at a closing?

The bill is for a calendar year and goes to the person who owned the property on January 1. The sheriff's page says a closing agent or attorney usually works out each side's share, then either pays the sheriff at the table or gives one party a credit on the settlement statement and leaves the payment to them.

The sheriff will not take a pro rated payment, so one or both parties must send the full amount. After a transfer, bills normally go in care of the new owner, though a sale near the print date may miss the update. If a bill reaches your old address, forward it to the buyer.

What permits matter before a Hardin County listing?

The Planning and Development Commission, created by the fiscal court in 1979, serves unincorporated Hardin County, including Glendale, Cecilia, Rineyville, Stephensburg and Colesburg. A building permit application needs an aerial photo of the property showing the structure and its distance from each property line. Sellers who built a deck, shed or addition without a permit can ask the commission's office whether it is on file before a buyer's inspector asks.

Houses inside Elizabethtown, Radcliff and the other cities are handled by those cities' offices.

What if a Hardin County bill goes delinquent?

When April 15 passes, unpaid bills move to the County Clerk. Call 270-765-2171 for the figure. The Department of Revenue illustrates the climb: a $1,000 bill becomes $1,254 on transfer, then collects monthly interest and clerk and attorney commissions. The clerk's website carries a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information.

An owner with back taxes can still close, because the title company pays the certificate out of the proceeds. Owners who would rather skip repairs and a listing can ask a cash buyer for an offer and compare it with the payoff.

More questions about Hardin County, KY Property Tax Guide

What is the discount period on Hardin County bills for 2026?

The sheriff lists November 1 through November 30, 2026. Face amount runs December 1 through 31, and penalties begin in January 2027.

Can I pay a Hardin County bill in installments?

No. The sheriff states that current year bills cannot be paid in part. One check may cover several bills if a copy of each is attached.

What does a card payment cost in Hardin County?

2.49 percent of the bill, online or at the sheriff's office. A mailed check to 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, avoids the fee.

Whom do I call for a payoff on an old Hardin County bill?

The County Clerk at 270-765-2171. Delinquent prior year bills are held there, and the clerk's website has a calculator.

Which Hardin County cities charge their own tax?

The 2026 schedule lists Elizabethtown, Radcliff, Sonora, Upton, Vine Grove and West Point. For districts 03 and 06 the sheriff points payers to Radcliff and Vine Grove for the separate city bill.

Madison County by the numbers

Who answers questions about a Madison County, KY tax bill?

Three Richmond offices split the work. The sheriff answers for the bill, the PVA answers for the value behind it, and the County Clerk answers for deeds and for overdue bills.

  • Sheriff: 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, reached at 859-623-1511. Bills can be searched and paid through a secure portal, at the counter, or by post, and cash should never go in an envelope.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption paperwork. The sheriff's tax page lists 859-623-5410 for it.
  • Clerk: deeds are filed at the Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave. The Berea branch at 304 Chestnut Street serves vehicle and marriage license customers.

An heir or agent can settle a bill ahead of a sale too, because KRS 134.119 lets the sheriff accept money from a third party for the owner.

Why does Madison County differ from the rural counties around it?

Madison County is a college county that has been adding residents for decades. Eastern Kentucky University is in Richmond, Berea College is in Berea, and Berea and Richmond are the county's only cities. Census counts show the effect: 28,541 people in 1940, 53,352 in 1980, 82,916 in 2010 and 92,701 in 2020, with the July 2025 estimate at 101,696.

The Transylvania Company bought some 20,000,000 acres west of the Appalachians from the Cherokee in 1774, and hired Daniel Boone to cut a trail through the Cumberland Gap and found a settlement on the Kentucky River. Settlement of the area began in the 1770s, and the county itself dates to December 1785, honoring James Madison. Fort Boonesborough, begun in April 1775, is today a state historic site. Interstate 75, U.S. 25, U.S. 421 and KY 52 cross the county, which borders Fayette County to the north and Jessamine, Garrard, Rockcastle, Jackson, Estill and Clark counties around the rest of its edge.

The 2020 census found 36,148 households, with renters in 40.5 percent of occupied units and 8.1 percent of all units vacant. Roughly 36 percent of residents were rural, which means plenty of sellers own land around Kingston, Waco or Speedwell rather than inside a city.

Appraisal of a farm follows what its soil earns, and a subdivision developer's offer plays no part. That is the rule in Section 172A of the state constitution. Ask the PVA to show how each of your acres is classified before you price a farm.

How big is the Madison County housing market?

Madison County has 42,389 housing units, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $232,000 in the 2020 to 2024 survey.

Madison County at a glance, from Census Bureau QuickFacts

Between the April 2020 base and July 2025 the county added 9.7 percent. Its 1,808 employer establishments paid about $1.19 billion in 2023, and shoppers spent $1.76 billion in stores during 2022. A broadband subscription reaches 88.9 percent of households.

Median age at the 2020 census was 35.6 years, and 20.4 percent of today's residents are under 18 against 16.1 percent who are 65 or older. The county grew 27.6 percent in the 1970 count and 24.9 percent in 1980. Veterans number 5,522. Households run 2.43 people, and 84.2 percent of residents stayed at the same address for the past year. Per capita income is $32,828, and 16.4 percent of residents fall below the poverty line. Land is getting busier: 212.0 people per square mile in 2020 against 189.6 in 2010.

When does a Madison County tax bill start costing extra?

The sheriff's tax page gives no fixed calendar. It tells owners to trust the periods shown on their own bill or in the portal. The ordinary timetable sits in KRS 134.015.

  • Paying everything by November 1 earns two percent off.
  • The following two months, through December, call for the face amount.
  • During January a five percent charge appears.
  • From February onward the charge is ten percent of the unpaid tax.

A late-printed bill gets a compressed schedule from the Department of Revenue, counted from the mailing date. Fees pile onto delinquent bills, and the state's collection guide adds one percent interest per month after the transfer to the clerk.

On the Clerk's website you will find the 2025 delinquent county property tax list, split in two parts and marked updated August 31, 2026, along with a third-party purchaser page. Search for your parcel before you list. The County Attorney's office also runs delinquent collection and says an installment agreement signed before the Clerk's sale keeps a bill from being bought by an investor. Its number is 624-4777, extension 9.

What is the route for disputing a Madison County valuation?

A sit-down with the PVA comes first. When it settles nothing, you file a petition at the Clerk's office and the county board takes the case, as laid out in KRS 133.120 which the legislature revised effective July 15, 2026. Carry sales data, an appraisal or insurance records, and keep paying on your own number during the dispute.

Close to either campus, nearby recent sales of similar houses make the strongest comparables. On acreage, ask which agricultural class the PVA applied. KRS 133.030 has the board meet between 25 and 35 days following inspection.

Does Madison County offer a senior or disability homestead exemption?

It does. The deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, which would lower a $232,000 home to a taxable $182,900. It is open to owner-occupants who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the Madison County PVA takes the application. A buyer who qualifies files separately after closing.

What should be settled before a Madison County closing?

Get a payoff figure from the sheriff for this year's bill and scan the clerk's delinquent list for earlier years. The sheriff's page notes that property taxes are commonly prorated between buyer and seller, with the current owner answerable for payment, so check how your settlement statement divides the bill.

A tax lien can ride with the land for as long as eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), which is why title agents ask for payoff at the table.

Deeds go to the Clerk's Richmond Branch at (859) 624-4703, extension 3. The office keeps papers from 1786 onward, searchable by a person's name only, and has scanned everything since 1986 for viewing in person or through the paid ECCLIX service. Electronic filings are handled each morning until roughly 10:00. Owners can also enroll in DocAlert, a free notification that fires whenever a document is recorded under their name or property details. The state's transfer tax, fifty cents for each $500 of value under KRS 142.050, comes to $232 at the Census median value.

More questions about Madison County, KY Property Tax Guide

Can Madison County property tax be paid online?

Yes, through the sheriff's secure portal, which also lets you search bills. The portal displays any processing fee before you confirm, and paying at the Richmond office or by mail still works.

How large is the 2026 exemption for Madison County seniors?

$49,100, the same as for 2025. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply through the PVA.

Which Madison County office records a deed?

The Clerk's Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, for the recordings desk.

Is there help when a Madison County bill has gone delinquent?

The County Attorney's delinquent tax program, at 624-4777 extension 9, can arrange installment payments if you sign before the Clerk's sale.

Who pays the Madison County tax bill when a house changes owners mid-year?

The sheriff says the current owner must make sure it is paid and that bills are commonly prorated at closing. Confirm the split with your closing agent.

Laurel County by the numbers

Which Laurel County offices does a tax bill pass through?

Three offices in and around London split the job. Valuation sits with the PVA, payment with the sheriff, and leftovers with the clerk. Calling the wrong one costs a seller time, so here is who does what.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): Room 127 at 101 S. Main St. Call (606) 864-2889. The office closes at 4:30 Monday through Friday, and its website runs parcel searches by street address, owner name or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192. Call 606-864-6600. Counter service ends at 4:00 on weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are closed.
  • County Clerk: Room 203 at the same Main Street address, phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk receives delinquent bills and runs the sale of the liens.

The rate differs by taxing district, so get the figure for your own parcel from the sheriff or the PVA.

What should an owner know about Laurel County itself?

Kentucky created Laurel County in December 1825 from four older counties. Today its land area measures about 434 square miles. London is the seat. Corbin lies mostly across the border in Whitley County. The county includes part of the Daniel Boone National Forest as well as a stretch of Laurel River Lake. History buffs know it for the Civil War fight at Wildcat Mountain, and visitors for the first Kentucky Fried Chicken cafe north of Corbin and the World Chicken Festival in London.

  • Population: an estimated 63,746 in July 2025, up from 62,613 in 2020 and 58,849 in 2010, with a 2020 density of 144 residents per square mile.
  • Older and disabled residents: 19.1 percent are 65 or above and 16.6 percent of under-65 residents report a disability, which are the groups the homestead exemption below serves.
  • Housing: 27,063 units, 23,996 households, 71.6 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value $159,500. With a mortgage, owners' median monthly cost is $1,239. Without one it is $382.
  • The Census Bureau counted 21 building permits for the county in 2025.
  • Jobs: 1,272 employer establishments and 23,992 workers in 2023, with retail sales near $1.68 billion in 2022.
  • Money and movement: median household income of $57,771, a 22.6 minute average commute, and 2.57 people per household.

What are the Laurel County payment dates and penalties?

The assessment date is New Year's Day, and the tax for that year is due at the sheriff's office before December 31 ends. KRS 134.015 turns the calendar into money.

  • Anyone who clears the full amount by November 1 pays 2 percent less.
  • November 2 through December 31 means paying the printed total.
  • January adds 5 percent on top.
  • From February, the add-on is 10 percent.

If bills are late getting out, the state can swap in a shifted timetable with a discount month followed by a face-value month. The sheriff's page lists three routes: walk in, mail a check, or leave one in the box on the building's front. Cards work at the office only. Cash does not belong in either, and a mailed receipt needs an envelope you have addressed and stamped.

How can a Laurel County owner contest a value?

Start by talking to the PVA or a deputy, since the local board will not hear an owner who skipped that step. Each May the roll of real property is open for public viewing, starting on the first Monday and lasting thirteen days with Saturdays included. The clerk's office accepts the written appeal until closing time on the first workday after the viewing days end.

The board convenes about a month after viewing ends. Useful proof includes comparable sales, an insurance policy, construction costs, or a description of the lot. Appeals that arrive without documents get denied, and a no-show at the hearing forfeits any later claim to the Kentucky Claims Commission. A bill printed before the dispute ends uses the owner's number, and the board's higher value would trigger a supplemental bill.

Who gets homestead relief in Laurel County?

For 2025 and 2026 the exemption is $49,100 of assessed value. A house assessed at $200,000 ends up taxable at $150,900. Eligible owners are at least 65 years old or classified as totally disabled. With so many older residents, a share of Laurel County sellers may have it on file already.

Applications are filed at the PVA's Room 127 office, along with documents showing age or disability. A claim based on disability is renewed yearly. Disability claimants renew each year, except service connected veterans and owners whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has already ruled permanently and totally disabled. Ask the PVA how the exemption is treated after the house is sold.

What does a delinquent Laurel County tax bill turn into?

On April 15 the sheriff's collection season ends. Open bills pass to the clerk, who files a lien and calls each a certificate of delinquency. A 1 percent monthly interest charge starts, and even a few days into a month counts as the whole month. The state's sample bill is $1,000. At the handoff it stands at $1,254 on an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, and every later step adds interest plus commissions for the clerk and county attorney.

Cost of a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill the longer it sits at the clerk (Department of Revenue samples; the last column is the gain over the handoff total)
Payment pointTotalGain
Handoff from sheriff$1,254.00none
Inside five business days$1,387.79$133.79
Following the first county attorney letter$1,611.30$357.30
Month two, in May$1,627.61$373.61
Once listed in the June newspaper$1,659.90$405.90
Taken over by a buyer at the sale$1,704.21$450.21

The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second within 60 days, and the second names the sale date. The clerk sets the sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and an outside buyer of the certificate can add hefty fees of its own. The Laurel County Clerk's notice for the 2026 sale had outside buyers registering August 17 through August 31 with a deposit of 25 percent of their list value, and that registration window is over. The same notice set the 2026 sale lottery for September 9 at 9:00 a.m. in the clerk's Delinquent Tax Department, also past. KRS 134.015 lets that lien last eleven years, whoever holds title.

What tax steps should a Laurel County seller finish before listing?

  • Get a statement from the sheriff showing this year's bill and any older year still open.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate already exists against the parcel.
  • Check the PVA website to confirm owner name, parcel number and assessed value.
  • Use the bill search links on the sheriff's website to pull the parcel's tax history, and bring the printout to the listing appointment.
  • If you hold the homestead exemption, ask the PVA what happens to it at the sale.
  • Spell out in the contract how this year's bill is divided so each side's share is clear to the closing agent.

A seller who prefers to avoid repairs can request a direct offer. Any balance due is deducted from the proceeds.

More questions about Laurel County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where does a Laurel County owner pay the tax bill?

At the sheriff's office, 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Payment is accepted at the counter with a card, by mailed check and at the drop box outside.

How big is the early payment discount in Laurel County?

Two percent off the bill, if the sheriff has full payment by November 1. From the next day through December the printed amount stands.

Which office handles a disagreement over value?

Start with the PVA's office at (606) 864-2889, because a meeting there is required before any appeal.

How much does the Kentucky homestead exemption take off?

Qualifying owners lose $49,100 of assessed value, and applications go to the PVA.

Does a tax lien stay with the property after a sale?

Yes. The lien under KRS 134.015 can run eleven years regardless of ownership, so a buyer's title agent looks for it.

Barren County by the numbers

How are Barren County, Kentucky property taxes set and collected?

In Barren County the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assesses each parcel, the fiscal court and other districts set rates, and the Barren County Sheriff mails the bills and takes payment from November through April. A disagreement about value goes to the PVA, while a payment question goes to the sheriff.

The county is 500 square miles of south central Kentucky. Glasgow is the seat and the largest city, joined by Cave City and Park City. Barren was carved out of Warren and Green counties in 1798 and is named for the Barrens, the grassland across its northern third. Interstate 65 clips the northwest corner, and the Cave City interchange feeds traffic to Mammoth Cave National Park, so lodging and tourism shape part of the tax base there while farming and Glasgow's factories carry the rest.

When does the Barren County Sheriff take tax payments?

The sheriff's property tax page says the office takes payments from November until April each year, and it asks you to bring your bill so the payment lands on the right account. Kentucky's standard calendar gives a 2 percent discount through November 1, and penalties begin after December 31.

Pay at the sheriff's office, by mail with the top portion of the bill attached, or online. The portal charges $1.50 per bank ACH payment and roughly 2.75 percent on cards. Enclose a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt by mail. The sheriff's page puts the duty on the taxpayer to know which bills are owed, a point that matters to anyone with a rental, a second parcel or a mobile home.

Calendars can shift in years when bills run late, so ask the office for the discount deadline that applies to your bill.

How is a Barren County assessment disputed?

No appeal can start in Barren County until you have spoken with the PVA. When the two of you cannot settle on a number during the roll inspection period, you can ask the county board of assessment appeals to decide by filing at the clerk's office the next business day after the period closes.

The three member board sits 25 to 35 days after inspection ends, and the state says it must deny an appeal where the owner offers no facts. Collect recent sales of similar houses near yours, and request the sales list the PVA used on your parcel during the conference. A certified letter brings the result, with the steps for a further appeal.

What do the Barren County numbers say about home values?

Census data describes a county of modest prices and middling incomes. The rows below come from the Barren County column of QuickFacts.

Barren County housing and income figures

At $178,000 the typical owned home is well under the $277,300 reported for Boone County in northern Kentucky. A lower price brings a smaller tax bill in dollars, and also a thinner margin when back taxes, repairs and a loan payoff all come out of one sale price.

Which Barren County owners can claim the homestead exemption?

Yes, if you are 65 or older or totally disabled and the house is your home. File on the state form with the Barren County PVA, and the approved amount comes off the assessed value.

KRS 132.810 treats a mobile home or manufactured house as a residential unit, which matters in a county this rural. The dollar figure moves with the cost of living every two years, so ask the PVA what applies to your year. When the property is sold, the owner or an executor reports the transfer to the PVA, and the next owner files a new application.

What follows an unpaid Barren County tax bill?

After April 15 the bill leaves the sheriff's office for the county clerk, which records a lien. Interest accrues monthly at 1 percent, with commissions for the clerk and the county attorney stacked on top. Letters follow, and the clerk lists delinquent parcels publicly before a summer sale to private buyers.

Under KRS 134.015 the tax is a personal debt of the owner and the lien can outlast a change of ownership by up to 11 years. A Barren County seller should ask for a written payoff from the sheriff before April 15 or from the clerk afterward, because the number changes from month to month.

What drives Barren County housing demand?

Barren County is mostly rural, with farming the main industry, but Glasgow adds manufacturing plants, a hospital and a Western Kentucky University campus, and it serves as the medical and retail center for the area. Wikipedia reports that a Kingspan data center infrastructure plant announced in Glasgow in 2026 is expected to bring 400 manufacturing jobs, the largest announcement in nearly two decades.

  • Cave City and Park City draw visitors who come for Mammoth Cave, Diamond Caverns and the roadside caves along the corridor.
  • Barren River Lake and its state resort park, on the Allen County line, support lake area homes and cabins.
  • The Glasgow Highland Games and the US 68 yard sales fill local lodging each June.

Roads matter to buyers here. Besides Interstate 65, the county has US 31E, US 31W and US 68, a CSX rail line through Cave City and Park City, and weekday bus service inside Glasgow. A house on a through route near the interstate interchange values differently from a farm tract on a back road, which is why the PVA's neighborhood sales data decides much of an assessment.

Three school systems divide the county: Barren County Schools, Glasgow Independent and Caverna Independent. Ask the sheriff which district appears on your bill.

Which Barren County offices matter before a sale?

Beyond the PVA, the clerk and the sheriff, the fiscal court's department list names offices that touch a sale. A building and electrical inspector, reached at (270) 651-3921, answers permit questions for additions and rewiring. The county floodplain administrator can say whether a parcel near Barren River Lake or a creek sits in a mapped flood zone. A joint city and county planning commission, at (270) 659-0661, handles zoning.

  • Check who is the owner of record and whether an exemption sits on the parcel.
  • Ask the sheriff whether other parcels carry your name, such as a vacant lot or a mobile home.
  • If the house passed through an estate, check that the clerk shows a clean recorded deed.
  • Update your mailing address with the sheriff so later notices reach you.

An owner in a hurry, with taxes owed or a house needing work, can set a cash offer beside a listing in which the bill is cleared at closing.

More questions about Barren County, KY Property Tax Guide

When is the Barren County tax season?

The sheriff collects from November until April. Kentucky's standard calendar gives a 2 percent discount through November 1, but ask the office for the dates on your bill.

Can Barren County tax be paid on the internet?

Yes, through the link on the Barren County Sheriff's property tax page. The sheriff lists $1.50 for bank ACH payments and about 2.75 percent for credit or debit cards.

Where does a Barren County valuation dispute begin?

A conference with the Barren County PVA. State law requires it before an appeal, and it takes place during the roll inspection period that opens in early May.

Does a mobile home earn the Barren County exemption?

It can. KRS 132.810 treats a mobile home or manufactured house as a residential unit when the owner lives there and is 65 or older or totally disabled.

Can delinquent Barren County tax stop a sale?

No. The lien stays with the property, so the payoff is settled from the seller's proceeds at closing. Ask for the amount in writing before accepting an offer.

Bullitt County by the numbers

What is Bullitt County, Kentucky, like for a home seller?

Bullitt County is the Louisville suburb that grew into a distribution hub. It sits just south of Jefferson County, with Spencer, Nelson and Hardin counties on its other sides, and covers 300 square miles in the Knobs region of the western Bluegrass. Shepherdsville is the county seat and the oldest town. Mount Washington is the largest city, and ten miles of Kentucky 44 link the two with homes along nearly the whole stretch.

Interstate 65 runs through the middle of the county. More than six million square feet of distribution and warehouse space has been built since 2000, with business parks about 16 miles from Louisville's airport and the UPS Worldport. The western fifth of the county, about 62 square miles, belongs to Fort Knox training land. UofL Health South Hospital opened in Shepherdsville in March 2024, and Bernheim Arboretum and Research Forest in Clermont is a visitor draw. The county's tourism impact was estimated at $173.2 million for 2025.

Bullitt's Lick, a salt lick near the Salt River, supplied Kentucky's first industry until around 1830, and the county was organized from parts of Jefferson and Nelson counties by an act approved December 13, 1796.

How do Bullitt County housing numbers compare?

Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population at 86,454, up 5.1 percent from 82,224 in the April 2020 base. The housing figures run higher than in nearby rural counties:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $247,200 (2020 to 2024), the highest of Boyle, Bracken, Breckinridge and Bullitt.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 84.9 percent across 31,747 households.
  • Median gross rent: $987, and median owner cost with a mortgage $1,561 a month.
  • Median household income: $80,558, with 8.5 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 654, against 34,722 housing units.

The 2020 count found 31,409 households, a median age of 40.3, and 70.5 percent of residents in urban areas. Monthly owner costs in the middle are $524 for owners without a mortgage, and 93.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. About 18.7 percent of residents are 65 or older, which is the group the homestead exemption serves, and 92.1 percent of households have broadband. The county counts 4,923 veterans. The mean commute is 28.7 minutes. Transportation and warehousing receipts in 2022 reached $327.8 million, which fits a county where trucking and logistics employ many residents. Density is 276.8 people per square mile.

Which Bullitt County office collects the property tax?

The Sheriff's Office takes the money and distributes it to the state, county, schools and special districts. Its office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville, phone 502-543-2514, and it collects over $170 million a year. Mail goes to PO Box 205, Shepherdsville, KY 40165. Between October 1 and December 31 you can also pay by check at any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county.

Assessments belong to the PVA, whose county annex office is at 149 North Walnut Street, phone 502-543-7480. The County Clerk, at 502-955-6369, gives payoff figures for delinquent bills from earlier years.

What are the Bullitt County tax dates?

The sheriff receives the bills from the clerk at the end of September and most owners see them in the first week of October. The 2026 bills list four due dates, by receipt or postmark:

  • November 1: face value less a 2 percent discount.
  • December 31: face value.
  • January 31: face value plus a 5 percent penalty.
  • April 15: face value plus a 21 percent penalty.

After April 1, the sheriff no longer accepts personal or business checks. Pay with cash, a certified check, a money order or a card. Card fees are set by the processor. Partial payments are refused, and an owner who has not received a bill by mid-October should call for a duplicate.

What is the Bullitt County tax rate for 2026?

The sheriff publishes a rate chart for each jurisdiction. The chart lists these 2026 real estate rates by jurisdiction, and the state line of 10.30 matches the cents-per-$100 form Kentucky uses.

2026 Bullitt County real estate rates by jurisdiction (source: Bullitt County Sheriff)

The first six lines add up to 100.30. The Nichols, Southeast and Zoneton fire districts are each 10.0, and a Plum Creek water line of 1.0 applies to real estate in its area. Shepherdsville's own tax comes combined with the county bill. Other incorporated places, including Mount Washington, Hillview, Hunters Hollow, Pioneer Village, Fox Chase, Lebanon Junction and Hebron Estates, bill their own city tax, so call the city. The tax district code on the bill tells you which applies.

Which Bullitt County school district applies?

Bullitt County Public Schools serves nearly the whole county and accounts for the largest line on the bill at 73.10. The Department of Defense Education Activity runs the schools on Fort Knox, including Fort Knox Middle High School. The county's high schools are Bullitt Central in Shepherdsville, Bullitt East in Mount Washington, North Bullitt in Hebron Estates and Riverview. Bernheim, Bullitt Lick, Eastside, Hebron, Mount Washington and Zoneton run the middle schools.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Bullitt County?

An owner who is 65 or older on January 1 and lives in the home can reduce the assessment by up to $49,100. The sheriff's page tells owners to bring proof of age, such as a driver's license, to the PVA with the application before paying. A totally disabled owner qualifies under the state rule as well. The application goes to the PVA by December 31 of the tax year.

How does an assessment appeal work in Bullitt County?

Request a conference at the PVA once the notice arrives. The tax roll is open for inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May, and a filing at the County Clerk is due the workday after the inspection period ends. The board of assessment appeals sits for as many as five days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring comparable sales and photos, because the board decides on evidence and a case with none is denied.

How should a Bullitt County seller handle the tax at closing?

The bill goes to the January 1 owner. A house that sells in the spring is still billed to the seller, and the closing agent divides the year between the parties. The sheriff requires the full bill to be paid, so the settlement statement must show who pays. Anything unpaid after April 15 moves to the clerk with a lien, and interest runs 1 percent a month; ask for a payoff before the closing date. Sellers with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses can often close with a cash buyer and have the tax paid from proceeds.

Call 502-543-2514. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville.

When does the Bullitt County 2% discount end?

For the 2026 bills it ends November 1, by receipt or postmark. December 31 is face value, January 31 adds 5 percent, and April 15 adds 21 percent.

Can I pay Bullitt County taxes at a bank?

Yes. Any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments from October 1 to December 31 during business hours.

Does Shepherdsville charge a separate city tax?

No separate bill. Shepherdsville's tax is combined with the county bill, while other cities such as Mount Washington and Hillview bill their own city tax.

How much is the Bullitt County homestead exemption?

Up to $49,100 off the assessed value for owners 65 or older who live in the home on January 1. Apply at the PVA before paying the bill.

Selling in Bourbon County?

Who sets and who collects property tax in Bourbon County, Kentucky?

Two offices in the Paris courthouse building split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) in Room 15 sets the value. The Sheriff's Office in Room 104 sends the bills and takes the money.

The county directory lists the PVA at (859) 987-2152, extension 217, and the sheriff at (859) 987-2130. Both offices open at half past eight on weekdays and close at four-thirty. The sheriff's page adds that the office shuts on holidays such as Good Friday, Memorial Day, Veterans Day and Thanksgiving.

How big is Bourbon County, and what does that mean for assessments?

Bourbon County covers roughly 290 square miles of mostly open, rolling farmland around Paris, with Millersburg and North Middletown as the smaller towns. Census figures put the population at 20,243 in 2025 and the housing stock at 9,399 units.

Home values here run well above neighboring Boyd County's $130,700 median. Typical home value is $229,300 and the owner-occupied share is 63.7%, both Census Bureau estimates. A seller with acreage can ask the PVA in Room 15 for the parcel record and compare it with a recent local sale before assuming the figure is right.

When are Bourbon County property taxes due?

The Sheriff's Office collects from November 1 through April 15. Paying sooner costs less, and the sheriff honors a U.S. postmark as the payment date.

Bourbon County Sheriff's posted collection periods
PeriodWhat applies
November 1 to November 302% discount
December 1 to December 31Base amount due
January 1 to January 315% penalty
February 1 to April 1521% penalty period

Delinquent notices are mailed February 1. When April 15 ends, every unpaid bill leaves the sheriff's hands for the County Clerk, and the sheriff warns that significant extra fees follow. A spring seller should find out whether the bill has already moved.

How do I pay a Bourbon County tax bill?

Pay at the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or mail a check to that address. Bills are mailed to the homeowner as postcards, so a seller whose mortgage company pays from escrow should ask the lender whether it needs a copy.

  • Accepted: cash, cashier's checks, money orders, and personal or business checks drawn on U.S. banks.
  • Cards are taken in person only, with a 3.5% fee. The sheriff's own example is $55.13 on a $1,575 bill.
  • Third party checks and foreign funds are refused.
  • A returned check carries a $50 fee, and a bill paid with a bad check counts as unpaid.

Can I dispute a Bourbon County assessment?

Yes. Assessments reflect January 1, and no forms come first: you ask the PVA or a deputy for a conference.

KRS 133.120 governs the steps. Request the conference while the May inspection window is open, which is a two-week stretch that the state can lengthen for a county. Still disagree? Write to the County Clerk with your reasons and what you believe the property is worth, and the clerk routes the letter to the board of assessment appeals. The deadline is one workday after the window closes. At the hearing, bring evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal or a contractor's repair quote.

Filing never stops the bill. Pay on the value you claim. If the board lands higher, the gap is billed later with interest. Skipping the county board closes the door on the state-level Board of Tax Appeals.

Is there a homestead exemption in Bourbon County?

Yes, the statewide one. Owners who reach age 65, or who are classed as totally disabled, can claim it. The state's deduction is $49,100 for the two years covering 2025 and 2026.

Applications go to the PVA in Room 15. Take a $200,000 assessment. After the deduction, tax is figured on $150,900. A disability claim is refiled every year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. Ask the PVA which figure your bill uses, because the amount is reset every two years.

What should I bring when I pay at the Bourbon County Sheriff's Office?

Bring the postcard bill or the parcel details, plus a payment the office accepts. Checks go out to the Bourbon County Sheriff's Office, and the sheriff's page lists the closings that matter for timing: Martin Luther King Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's.

  • Count a mailed check as paid on its postmark date, and mail early in November to keep the discount.
  • Skip online payment: the sheriff states the office offers neither online nor phone payment.
  • Check that the check is drawn on a U.S. bank and is not made out by a third party.

What does a late Bourbon County tax bill cost in real dollars?

Take a bill of $2,000. Paid during November it is $1,960 after the 2% discount. In December it is $2,000. In January the 5% penalty makes it $2,100, and from February 1 through April 15 the 21% period brings it to $2,420. That is a $460 spread between paying in November and waiting until the last collection day.

The sheriff posts that last stretch as a 21% penalty period, and the 21% is the figure used above. After April 15 the County Clerk adds its own fees, and the amount you owe is whatever the clerk quotes on the day you pay. Sellers with an unpaid bill from a past year should call the clerk for that number before setting a closing date.

What do other Bourbon County figures show about the housing market?

The county issued 109 building permits in 2025, far more than Boyd County's 12, and retail sales per person in 2022 were $39,822. Median household income was $61,354 for 2020 to 2024, and 13.9% of residents were in poverty. The Census Bureau finds 94.9% of residents in the same house they occupied a year before. Turnover is low, and listings stay few.

That steadiness helps a seller who has the paperwork in order. A buyer's lender or title company will want the current tax bill, the deed and any lien releases on the table at closing, and each of those comes from an office within one building at 301 Main Street.

What becomes of the tax bill when a Bourbon County house sells?

Unpaid tax becomes a charge on the house itself, while the debt belongs to whoever owned it on the January 1 assessment date. The closing agent will confirm the bill is current.

  • Check with the sheriff on whether this year's bill is paid and in which collection period.
  • Give the buyer's mailing address in the deed's tax-bill line so the next postcard finds them.
  • Agree with the buyer on how this year's tax is split.
  • For a past-due year, expect the clerk, not the sheriff, to quote the payoff.

Typical owner costs run $1,424 a month with a mortgage and $466 without one, so the tax bill is one piece of a larger monthly picture.

More questions about Bourbon County, KY Property Tax Guide

What is the deadline to avoid a penalty on a Bourbon County bill?

December 31 is the last day for the plain face amount. The 2% discount ends November 30, and the 5% penalty begins January 1.

Where can I hand over a Bourbon County tax payment?

At the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or by mail to that address. Card payments are accepted only in person, with a 3.5% fee.

What happens to a Bourbon County bill unpaid after April 15?

The sheriff passes it to the County Clerk, and the sheriff's page says significant added fees apply.

How do I appeal my Bourbon County property assessment?

Begin with a PVA conference in May. If it fails, send the County Clerk a written petition the workday after the inspection window closes.

Who is eligible for the Bourbon County homestead exemption?

Owners aged 65 and up, plus owners classed as totally disabled, who file with the PVA. The state's deduction is $49,100 across 2025 and 2026.

McCracken County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky

  • McCracken County, KY Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a McCracken County, KY Property Tax Guide sale

Who to contact in McCracken County

Tax rate

Mccracken County by the numbers

Which McCracken County offices touch a tax bill?

Three do, each with its own lane. A parcel's dollar value is the work of the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). The Sheriff's Office receives the payment. Only after the spring cutoff does the County Clerk get involved, and then only for bills still open. The PVA's website says outright that it neither mails bills nor accepts payments, so a check carried to the assessment office will be turned around.

You will find the PVA at 621 Washington Street in Paducah. Weekday hours run eight to four-thirty, and callers can dial (270) 444-4712. Public service companies and a few similar accounts are valued in Frankfort by the state Revenue Cabinet instead. For payments, see the Sheriff's tax page, which lists walk-in service Monday to Friday between 8:30 and 4:30 during collection season. County offices share the 300 Clarence Gaines Street address.

When can McCracken County taxes be paid, and what does waiting cost?

Collection by the Sheriff opens November 1 and closes April 15, and the county's delinquent-tax FAQ puts the mailing of notices in late September or early October. KRS 134.015 then prices each stage:

  • Settling the whole bill by November 1 earns 2 percent off, and that date for 2026 is behind us.
  • November 2 to year end: the printed figure, no more and no less.
  • Throughout January, add 5 percent.
  • Once January ends, the add-on doubles to 10 percent.
  • After April 15 the Sheriff hands over whatever is still open.

Mail, phone, counter and a website button (live November through April, per the office) all work. Anyone paying by card or e-check owes a processing charge to an outside vendor, which is shown before you confirm. If a lender escrows your tax, call it first, because the Sheriff sends a bill to the owner only, and the lender may already have requested its own copy.

How much will a McCracken County tax bill come to?

Frankfort's 2025 real property rate is 10.6 cents on each $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents the year before. Run that against the $188,100 Census median and you get about $199.39 for the state alone. The city, schools, library, fire districts and county each add a levy, and the PVA lists those same bodies as users of its assessments.

One line is newer than the rest: a county 911 fee that first appeared on the 2024 bills. Most parcels pay $46.26, the Sheriff says. The early-payment reduction skips that line, which matters when you estimate a credit at closing.

Snapshot of McCracken County homes and households from Census QuickFacts
ItemFigure
People living here, mid-202567,553
Share of homes occupied by owners68.9%
Typical owned-home value$188,100
Typical monthly rent$898
Typical household income$64,373
Building permits in 2025170

A house far from that middle point deserves a question to the PVA about how its value was built.

What steps does a McCracken County owner follow to contest a value?

Begin with a sit-down at the PVA office, since nothing can be filed before it. The dates after that are fixed by statute.

  • The roll lies open for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May.
  • Expect the PVA or a deputy to explain the valuation and write up what each side said.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk one business day after the viewing window shuts.
  • Gather proof for the hearing: insurance papers, building costs, land and structure descriptions, and sale listings. A claim with nothing attached is rejected.
  • A panel of local owners hears the case about a month later.

A hired representative has to be on the Revenue Department's list of eligible professionals, such as an attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, with your signed authorization. If bills are already out and the board lands above your claimed figure, a supplemental bill follows. The Sheriff adds a caution of its own: leaving new additions off the record can bring a 20 percent penalty on the bill.

Can older McCracken County owners lower the taxable value?

Yes. Owners 65 and over, and those found totally disabled, can take $49,100 off assessed value for both 2025 and 2026. The rate then applies only to what remains.

Take the $188,100 median: taxable value falls to $139,000, and the state's slice drops to about $147.34. Apply at the McCracken County PVA, not the Sheriff. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Claimants who rely on disability must have a federal or retirement-system finding, and most renew yearly. Veterans with a service-connected disability need not renew yearly, nor do people already ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or the state retirement systems. Nothing is granted until a formal application is on file, the PVA's site notes.

What becomes of an unpaid McCracken County bill when the house is sold?

It stays with the parcel. After April 15 the County Clerk holds it as a certificate of delinquency, records a lien, and charges 1 percent a month. KRS 134.420 lets the lien run 11 years through any change of owner, which means a buyer's title search will turn it up.

Delinquent bills go to the County Attorney, who works under a state agreement. Its letters warn that ignoring the bill can end in foreclosure, while an owner who keeps up an installment agreement has the bill marked unavailable for sale to investors. The Clerk's yearly sale of such bills is normally held in October. An investor who buys one must notify the owner within 50 days, may add its own charges, and can ask a court to foreclose after a year. Before listing, get a payoff figure from the Sheriff, and clear it before April 15 if you can.

What should a seller know about McCracken County itself?

The county spreads over 268 square miles at Kentucky's far western tip, part of the Jackson Purchase, with the Ohio River along its north and the Tennessee River along its northeast. It dates from 1825 and anchors the Paducah, KY-IL metropolitan area. Paducah, the seat, is the lone incorporated city. Farley, Hendron, Massac and Reidland are counted by the Census as designated places, and names such as Lone Oak, Heath and West Paducah show up as unincorporated communities.

Steamboats, barges and the Illinois Central made this a river-and-rail economy, and in the 1920s the railroad put its biggest operating and maintenance base anywhere here. Two districts teach the children: McCracken County Public Schools for nearly everywhere outside the city, and Paducah Public Schools for most of Paducah. West Kentucky Community and Technical College is in town. Clocks run on Central time, and the average worker travels 17.6 minutes to a job.

Owners live in about 69 percent of homes, and 170 permits in 2025 mean most sales involve an existing house. If yours carries unpaid tax, a lien or repairs you would rather skip, an investor paying cash for the house in its current condition can fold the tax payoff into one closing.

More questions about McCracken County, KY Property Tax Guide

Is the McCracken County PVA where I pay my tax?

No. The PVA handles values and exemptions only. Take payment to the Sheriff's Office.

What changes on April 15 for unpaid McCracken County taxes?

Sheriff collection of the prior bill ends that evening. Any balance heads to the County Clerk's office, and interest and fees begin to build.

Is the 911 fee on McCracken County bills eligible for the early-payment cut?

No. According to the Sheriff, the 911 fee that arrived with the 2024 bills sits outside the discount, and most parcels owe $46.26 for it.

How much is the homestead deduction for a McCracken County owner in 2026?

For 2026 the deduction is $49,100, as in 2025. Anyone 65 or older, or totally disabled, applies through the PVA.

Can I close on a McCracken County house that has back taxes?

Yes. The usual route is for the closing agent to pay the balance from the seller's proceeds, after you have asked the Sheriff or Clerk for a payoff.

Oldham County by the numbers

Oldham County's sheriff mails and collects the bill. Its valuation comes from the Property Valuation Administration (PVA). Envelopes are out by the end of September, and the sheriff can be reached at 502-222-9501.

The sheriff's site also carries a Property Tax FAQ for owners who want more detail on payment options. A value that looks wrong is a PVA matter, at 502-222-9320, because the sheriff never assigns value to any parcel. Each bill spells out when payment is due, how penalties are avoided and what a mortgage servicer's payment looks like.

Why does Oldham County stand out in Kentucky?

Oldham County lies in north central Kentucky as part of metropolitan Louisville. Wikipedia's county profile ranks it first in the state for both wealth and education. Its 196 square miles make it the 13th smallest county in Kentucky, with the Ohio River marking the northern line against Indiana.

Kentucky lawmakers formed it in 1823, using land from Henry, Jefferson and Shelby counties. Towns sprouted along the Louisville and Frankfort railroad during the 1850s, and Interstate 71, completed in the early 1970s, tied the county to downtown Louisville. La Grange is both the seat and the biggest city. Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff are cities too, and Buckner and Westport are census-designated places. Prospect lies mostly in Jefferson County, so check which county bills a Prospect parcel. Jefferson, Shelby, Henry and Trimble counties adjoin Oldham in Kentucky, with Clark County across the river in Indiana.

Growth shows in the head count: 14,687 people in 1970, 27,795 in 1980, 43,455 in 1990, 60,316 in 2010 and 67,607 in 2020. Students attend Oldham County Schools, which operates North Oldham High School, Oldham County High School and South Oldham High School, and one of the first questions buyers ask is which of the three serves an address.

How do the Oldham County numbers look?

Prices here run well beyond the Kentucky norm. The table's survey figures span 2020 to 2024.

An owner with a mortgage pays $2,193 a month at the median, against $712 without one. Poverty affects 6.0 percent of residents. The 23,025 households average 2.84 people, and seniors make up 17.1 percent of the population. In the 2020 census, 42.4 percent of households had children under 18 and the median age was 40.0.

When are Oldham County owners expected to pay?

Oldham County follows the statewide calendar in KRS 134.015. Pay by November 1 to save 2 percent, pay the printed amount through December, and expect a 5 percent penalty in January that becomes 10 percent afterward.

  • With escrow, verify the lender paid ahead of the discount deadline.
  • For a fall closing, get the title agent to say who pays the current bill.
  • In Crestwood, the city levy shows up on the sheriff's bill.

The owner on January 1 owes that year's tax, so a spring seller still gets the bill and splits it with the buyer at the closing table.

What can an Oldham County owner do about a high valuation?

The opening step, as a statewide PVA appeal guide describes it, is a PVA conference. Bring your own number and backing for it, such as nearby sales, a recent appraisal, contractor quotes or rent records.

If talks fail, the path leads through the Oldham County Clerk to a three-resident local board and finally to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, where the deadline is 30 days from the mailed ruling. At a $393,100 median, sales from the same subdivision make the strongest evidence.

Where do unpaid Oldham County bills end up?

Anything the sheriff has not collected by closing time on April 15 is handed to the County Clerk. The Oldham County Clerk's delinquent tax page refers value disputes to the PVA and sale questions to the Department of Revenue.

Under the state collection guide, the parcel is liened, interest runs at 1 percent monthly, the county attorney mails warnings, and any sale waits at least 90 days after the transfer. When an investor buys the certificate, the owner then owes the investor. If you are selling, get the clerk's quote and settle it from your proceeds.

Which charges land on an Oldham County seller at closing?

Kentucky's transfer tax is the seller's: fifty cents for each $500 of value, counting any remainder as a full $500, taken by the clerk with the deed (KRS 142.050). A $393,100 sale spans 787 units of $500 and owes $393.50. Spouse-to-spouse deeds, corrective deeds and foreclosure deeds are exempt.

  • Every deed lists the full price, mailing addresses for both sides and a forwarding address for the next tax bill.
  • A gift or token-price sale needs a sworn market-value estimate.
  • Heirs file the personal representative's affidavit wherever the estate holds land.

Who are Oldham County's neighbors and likely buyers?

The county packs in more people per acre than most of Kentucky. In 2010 the county averaged 322.2 people per square mile, and by 2020 it averaged 361.1. Veterans number 3,634. High school graduates account for 94.5 percent of adults, 4.2 percent of residents were born outside the United States, and 6.0 percent speak another language at home.

Most households stay put, with 88.4 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier. Just 4.3 percent of people under 65 have no health insurance, and 7.3 percent have a disability. Children make up 23.9 percent of residents, which is why school zones dominate buyer questions.

What is driving the Oldham County housing market?

Growth is steady. The county gained roughly 3,400 residents between April 2020 and July 2025, and builders took out 276 permits in 2025. Bachelor's degrees belong to 46.4 percent of adults, broadband reaches 95.4 percent of households, and a commute averages 26.2 minutes one way.

The jobs picture explains the pull: the county had 1,404 employer establishments and 14,369 jobs in 2023, with $775.1 million in payroll, and employment rose 6.2 percent from 2022 to 2023. A further 6,086 nonemployer businesses operated in 2024, and 64.1 percent of residents aged 16 or older are in the labor force. Retail sales hit $728.0 million in 2022. Health care and social assistance brought in $350.7 million. Wikipedia reports that 74.8 percent of residents lived in urban areas in 2020. The sheriff bills 18 special districts and one city, so neighbors a few miles apart can owe different totals. Check the districts on a bill before comparing listings.

More questions about Oldham County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who handles questions about an Oldham County valuation?

The PVA, 502-222-9320. Values come from that office, and the sheriff only collects what they produce.

When do Oldham County property tax bills arrive?

The sheriff's tax page says mailing wraps up by the end of September. Call 502-222-9501 if yours is missing in early October.

Is Crestwood's city tax billed separately?

No. The Crestwood levy rides on the same sheriff bill as the county and district charges, so a single payment covers all of them.

How much transfer tax applies to a median-priced Oldham County sale?

$393.50 on a $393,100 sale, owed by the seller and paid to the clerk before the deed is recorded.

Can a house with a tax lien on it still be sold in Oldham County?

Yes. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds.
