Table sources: Simpson County government and PVA pages.

More questions about Simpson County, KY Property Tax Guide

Does Franklin bill its own property tax?

Yes. Franklin sets rates through its commission and runs a tax office at 117 W Cedar, open weekdays until 4 p.m. Central time. Houses inside city limits get two bills, one from the county and one from the city.

Who is billed if I buy a Simpson County house after January 1?

The former owner is the taxpayer of record for that year. The PVA mails the bill to the new owner when it can, and a buyer who receives nothing can call the Sheriff at 270-586-7425.

When does the Simpson County early payment discount end?

On November 1. Full payment by then takes 2 percent off, and the face amount holds through December 31 under KRS 134.015. Penalties of 5 and then 10 percent follow.

Where is a Simpson County assessment appeal filed?

After a PVA conference, file with the County Clerk at 105 E Kentucky St. The conference has to happen while the roll is open for inspection, which starts in early May.

What deed tax comes out of a Simpson County sale?

Half a dollar per $500 of price, with a partial block counted whole, so a $229,400 sale owes $229.50 through the County Clerk at recording.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Taylor County

  • Taylor County Sheriff's Department

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Taylor County official site (taylorcountyky.gov) links its Property Valuation office to taylorpva.com
  • Kentucky law mandates sheriff collects property taxes; 2026 online payments via vendor cpteller.com and view.properlytaxes.com (id=47)

Selling in Taylor County?
We buy Taylor County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where do Taylor County property tax matters get handled?

Taylor County stacks its tax offices on one street in Campbellsville. The sheriff, the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) and the county clerk all work out of 203 North Court Street, so a single stop can cover a payoff, an exemption form and a lien check.

Taylor County tax offices in Campbellsville (sources: sheriff's page, PVA site, county clerk site)

Sheriff, current billsSuite 7; Monday to Friday 8:00 to 4:30; a drop box sits outside the door(270) 465-4351
PVA, values and exemptionsSuite 6; Monday to Friday 8:00 to 4:30(270) 465-5811
County clerk, delinquent bills and recordingMonday to Friday 8:00 to 4:30; Saturday 9:00 to noon(270) 465-6677

The sheriff's page also links an online portal for searching and paying 2026 bills. Pop-ups must be switched on in your browser or the portal will not open.

What is worth knowing about Taylor County before listing?

Taylor County became Kentucky's 100th county out of 120 when it was organized in 1848. Settlers arrived from Virginia, Pennsylvania, Maryland and North Carolina after the Revolution, and the name honors Zachary Taylor. Its 277 square miles, 266 of them land, take the outline of a heart, and local boosters say the geographic center of Kentucky sits inside. Neighboring counties dispute that. The Civil War skirmish known as the Battle of Tebbs Bend was fought here.

Campbellsville is the seat and the only city, with Acton, Hobson, Mannsville, Saloma and Spurlington among the unincorporated communities. Marion, Casey, Adair, Green and LaRue counties surround it. The Green and Adair lines also mark the Central time boundary, and Black Gnat straddles it. Campbellsville Independent and Taylor County Schools split the school districts. The 2020 count placed 49.1 percent of residents in urban areas, a share Spencer, Todd and Trigg counties did not have at all.

Headcount has risen steadily, from 7,251 in 1850 to 11,961 in 1910, 17,138 in 1970 and 26,023 in 2020, when the median age was 38.9. Campbellsville University anchors the economy. A study the university released in 2021 credited it with 1,866 local jobs and about $174.6 million of economic impact from its main campus. Census business data points the same way:

  • 2022 retail sales reached $1.09 billion, near $41,299 for every resident.
  • Medical and social-service providers took in $245.8 million.
  • 631 employers ran payrolls in 2023, with 9,968 workers between them.

How do Taylor County's housing numbers read?

The Census Bureau estimates 26,763 residents for July 2025, a 2.8 percent gain on 2020 and well above the 21,178 counted in 1980. Typical home value is $174,200 and typical rent is $718. Homeowners live in 68.8 percent of units, the lowest rate of the four counties, because a larger share rents: the 2020 census found 35.9 percent of occupied units were rentals, and 28.9 percent of households were one person living alone.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,217 a month for housing, against $432 for owners with none. Household income is $60,456 and the mean commute is 22.7 minutes. The Census Bureau logged just 9 building permits in 2025 against 11,247 housing units, so new construction adds little to the supply.

Who owns and who rents around Campbellsville?

The household picture explains why Taylor County is not a one-note market. Roughly one resident in five is past 65 (19.5 percent), and 23.1 percent are under 18. Per-person income of $28,896 is the lowest of the four counties, and the poverty rate stands at 16.4 percent. About 18.4 percent of residents under 65 live with a disability.

  • Households average 2.45 people, so many homes are small ones.
  • A bachelor's degree or more is held by 23.0 percent of adults, and 88.3 percent finished high school.
  • Transportation and warehousing receipts were $62.0 million in 2022, and accommodation and food sales were $51.8 million.

The 2020 census counted 10,171 households among 11,199 housing units, 9.2 percent of them vacant, and the rental vacancy rate was 5.8 percent.

What deadlines and surcharges apply to Taylor County bills?

State law sends payment to the sheriff, with a due date at the end of the assessment year. The sequence runs:

  • A bill settled by November 1 earns a 2 percent break.
  • Between that date and December 31, the printed amount applies.
  • January brings a 5 percent surcharge.
  • After January 31, 10 percent applies, with the sheriff's add-on fee from the Revenue Department's delinquency worksheet.

The clerk's website states that Taylor County bills turn delinquent on April 15 each year, when the sheriff's file closes and unpaid bills pass to the clerk.

What does the Taylor County clerk do with unpaid bills?

Collection moves to the clerk, with the county attorney writing to each owner. Two letters go out and the delinquent list runs in the Central Kentucky News Journal. A bill still open after those three notices can be offered to third-party companies, which buy it and place a lien against the land. The clerk says sales do not happen before August and that the list, with the sale date, is posted on the clerk's page as the day approaches.

The Revenue Department's worked example shows how fast a debt grows. In that sample a $1,000 bill turns into a $1,254 certificate once penalty, add-on fee and an assumed commission are included. Then 1 percent interest accrues monthly, with a 10 percent clerk commission and, after the first notice, a 20 percent county attorney commission. Paying within five business days of the transfer avoids the attorney's share.

How can I appeal a Taylor County assessment?

Meeting with the PVA at Suite 6 is the entry point. PVAs value most houses by comparing recent sales, and your conference is the time to ask which sales were used. After the meeting you file with the clerk at the end of the next workday after the May viewing period, a stretch of two weeks that includes Saturdays. A board of local owners hears the case roughly a month afterward.

Come with facts: building characteristics, insurance values, construction costs or listings of similar property. Without them the board denies the appeal. A paid representative needs your written authorization and a recognized credential, for example an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser.

Farmland follows a separate rule. Kentucky values it at what the land earns in agriculture rather than what it would sell for, which can cut a bill sharply near cities and matters less in rural areas where the two values sit close together. Taxable personal property is listed with the PVA by May 15.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Taylor County?

Owners past 65, or classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, have $49,100 subtracted from the assessment for 2025 and 2026. File Form 62A350 at the PVA before December 31. A household gets one exemption even if both spouses qualify, and a purchaser must apply again after a sale.

How do I clear Taylor County taxes before closing?

Get the sheriff's exact payoff, then ask the clerk whether the parcel carries a certificate from an earlier year. Each year's tax is the January 1 owner's own debt, and a delinquent lien can follow the land for eleven years. When an outside company holds the bill, the money goes to that company instead of the clerk.

More questions about Taylor County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where can I pay a Taylor County property tax bill?

At the sheriff's office, 203 North Court Street, Suite 7, or through the online portal for 2026 payments. Call (270) 465-4351 to confirm the amount.

When does a Taylor County bill turn delinquent?

On April 15 of the following year, according to the clerk's website. The sheriff's file closes and the clerk takes over collection.

Will Taylor County sell my overdue tax bill to a company?

It can, after the three notices. The clerk says no sales happen before August, and the buyer's lien then attaches to your property.

How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Taylor County?

Take Form 62A350 to the PVA at (270) 465-5811 before December 31. The home must be your residence on January 1, and you must qualify by age or disability.

Can I sell my Taylor County house with back taxes owed?

Yes. The payoff comes out of your sale money. Bring written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk so the closing agent can clear every open year.

Which offices run property tax in Adair County, KY?

Adair County divides the job between two offices. One of them, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), assigns each parcel its worth, while the sheriff is the one who receives payment. The rate itself is voted by the bodies that levy the tax, such as the fiscal court and the school board.

Find the PVA on Public Square in Columbia: 424 Public Square, Suite 2, KY 42728, telephone (270) 384-3673, weekdays eight to four. Deputies there process deed transfers, including partial sales, and adjust vehicle values. On the same contact page the county lists the sheriff at (270) 384-2776 and the County Clerk at (270) 384-2801.

Kentucky freezes the picture on January 1: a parcel is appraised as it was that morning. Anyone closing in February will usually find the year's bill addressed to the seller, so the Adair County sale contract ought to spell out who repays whom.

When must Adair County tax bills be paid?

The sheriff takes payment through every stage of the statutory calendar in KRS 134.015. The table shows what each stage costs.

Adair County bill payment stages, statewide schedule (source: KRS 134.015)
Payment windowWhat you owe
On or before November 1Face amount less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
After January 31Face amount plus 10 percent

If the state delays bill mailing, it may substitute a shifted calendar built on one-month blocks. Whatever remains unpaid at the end of the collection season, April 15 under the normal schedule, goes to the County Clerk with a recorded lien.

What would an Adair County owner actually pay?

Frankfort levies 10.6 cents for every $100 of assessed value in 2025, a cut from 10.9 cents in 2024. Put that against a $150,800 house, the Census midpoint for Adair County, and the state portion is roughly $159.85. Other taxing bodies add their own rates, so ask the PVA or the sheriff for the combined total on a given address.

The homestead exemption changes the math for older owners. If the assessment drops to $101,700 after the exemption, the state share falls to about $107.80. Paying early trims 2 percent off whatever the total turns out to be.

Those numbers matter in a sale because the year's bill has to be divided between buyer and seller somewhere. Ask the closing agent how the contract handles it, and ask the sheriff what has already been paid on the account.

How does an Adair County owner challenge a value?

An owner who wants to appeal must first confer with the PVA or a deputy. Public viewing of the roll starts on the first Monday in May and lasts through the following two weeks. Raise a disputed value then, or earlier if notices have already gone out.

  • The PVA is required to explain how your number was derived, and the meeting is documented in writing.
  • The appeal itself is filed at the County Clerk's office, with a deadline one workday after viewing wraps up.
  • Gather proof: descriptions of the land and buildings, insurance papers, building costs and comparable listings or sales. Without it the board turns the appeal down.
  • Attend the hearing, which comes a few weeks later. Filing and then not appearing forfeits later review by the Kentucky Claims Commission.

A paid representative has to fall into a listed category, for example an attorney, CPA, licensed broker or certified appraiser, and must bring your written authorization. If the board lands above the figure you claimed, you receive a supplemental bill for the gap.

Can an older Adair County owner reduce the tax base?

Yes, through the homestead exemption. People 65 and older, along with owners the law classes as totally disabled, receive a deduction that the state Revenue Department fixed at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply that to $150,800, the Census median home value here, and the taxed amount falls to $101,700.

File the form with the Adair County PVA during the year you want relief, by post, fax or email. The PVA accepts a driver's license, Medicare card or birth certificate as proof of age, with a Kentucky license or state ID covering residence. A household gets one exemption, and one spouse reaching 65 satisfies the age test.

Once approved, the exemption continues while the applicant stays in the home as owner. After a sale, the seller should notify the PVA so it is removed from the old address and can be requested for a new one.

What happens if I sell an Adair County house with taxes unpaid?

Selling does not erase an overdue balance. KRS 134.015 makes the tax the owner's own debt starting on the assessment date, and the parcel stays liened until payment or the expiry of the eleven-year span in KRS 134.420. A new deed does not change that. A title search will surface the lien, which is why the sheriff's payoff figure is worth getting before listing day.

While the County Clerk holds the account, each month adds 1 percent interest. The clerk and the county attorney take commissions, and a recording fee for the lien is added. Two notices go out by mail. Certificates can go on sale from 90 to 135 days after the handoff, and whoever buys one at that sale may add fees.

Paying the sheriff before April 15 avoids those clerk-stage extras completely.

What is Adair County, Kentucky, like for a seller?

Green County gave up part of its land in 1801 to create Adair County, whose lone municipality, Columbia, serves as seat. Roughly 405 square miles of land lie on the Pennyroyal Plateau, over 40 percent of it wooded. The Green River drains the county, and its impoundment as Green River Lake anchors a state park shared with Taylor County.

Farming drives the local economy: livestock, dairy, corn and tobacco. Road access improved a great deal once the Cumberland Parkway opened in 1973. Students attend Adair County Schools from the primary center to the high school. Census QuickFacts supplies these numbers:

  • 2025 population: 19,423, a gain of 2.8 percent over 2020.
  • Owner-occupied share of housing: 77.2 percent.
  • Home value at the midpoint: $150,800.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $53,553, and the poverty rate is 21.2 percent.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $771.

Neighbors on the map are Green, Taylor, Casey, Russell, Cumberland and Metcalfe counties. Columbia keeps Central time while Taylor and Casey counties to the north run on Eastern, a detail worth remembering when scheduling a closing with out-of-county parties. Rural areas hold 73.5 percent of the population, and the Census counted 7,136 households of 2.51 people on average.

The county recorded just six building permits in 2025, so nearly every sale involves a house that already stands. Where a house needs repairs or owes back taxes, selling for cash as-is lets both be cleared at a single closing.

More questions about Adair County, KY Property Tax Guide

When is the discount deadline for Adair County property taxes?

November 1 is the cutoff. Paying the whole bill by then saves 2 percent, the face amount applies from November 2 into December, and penalties start with the new year.

Who takes payment of Adair County tax bills?

Pay the Adair County Sheriff, whom the county lists at (270) 384-2776. The PVA, reachable at (270) 384-3673, only values property and never takes payments.

How much is the homestead exemption in Adair County?

The Department of Revenue fixed it at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 years, deducted from the assessed figure. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply at the PVA in Columbia.

Can I appeal my Adair County assessment after the deadline?

Not once the viewing period is over. The conference with the PVA must happen first, and the clerk filing is due the next workday after viewing ends. Viewing begins the first Monday of May and runs 13 days.

What happens if Adair County taxes go unpaid?

Once April 15 passes, the county clerk holds it as a certificate of delinquency backed by a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent monthly accrues, and the certificate may be sold between 90 and 135 days after the handoff.

Which Calloway County offices handle a Murray property tax bill?

Two offices share the work. The Property Valuation Administrator puts a value on the house, and the Sheriff's Office bills and collects. By the sheriff's own count, its tax desk processes over 27 thousand bills and more than 11 million dollars a year, so it is the main collector for Murray and the rural parts of the county alike.

Homestead and disability forms, and value questions, go to the PVA at 270-753-3482. Payments go to the tax office at 701 Olive Street. When the sheriff's season ends, delinquent bills pass to the county clerk, a hand-off the state revenue department describes step by step.

The county spans about 385 square miles of land on the state's southwest edge and held 37,103 people in 2020. Murray State University is in Murray, and with a large rental share the housing stock turns over differently here than in farm counties.

What does a late Calloway County tax payment cost?

KRS 134.015 gives early payers 2% off, then charges face value until December 31 and penalties after that. Calloway's twist is the early cutoff: the sheriff's page says a payment postmarked by November 15 earns the discount, two weeks sooner than Caldwell County's November 30.

Your bill carries its own dated schedule in the top right corner, and the amount climbs with each later date. Past the discount, the statewide steps apply:

  • Mid-November through December 31: the printed amount, no extras.
  • Throughout January: a 5% penalty.
  • Starting February 1: a 10% penalty and a sheriff's add-on fee.

The sheriff accepts cash, check, money order or an online card payment. A returned check carries a $50 fee, and penalties can apply again when you resend. The office asks customers not to mail cash.

Where and how do I pay in Murray?

Four routes work: a drop box, the mail, the counter or the website. The box on the west side of the building at 701 Olive Street never closes. Counter service runs weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., and the bill must come with you.

  • By mail: send the stub and a check to 701 Olive St., Murray, KY 42071, and add a stamped return envelope to get a receipt back.
  • Online: the sheriff's tax search page ends with a printable receipt.
  • Several bills at once: allowed by mail or at the counter if every stub is enclosed.
  • Questions: the tax office answers at (270) 761-4TAX.

Pay just the one "balance due" figure for your date. The sheriff cautions against splitting the payment among the state, county and school lines on the bill.

Who pays the tax when a Calloway County house sells?

The sheriff's FAQ describes a standard split: the seller covers a prorated slice of the year at closing, and the buyer pays the whole bill once it is issued. When unsure, read the settlement statement.

A sale that closes before billing leaves the title company to hold back an estimate. Ask the tax office for the current balance and whether an older year is open, since past-due taxes are paid at the clerk, not the sheriff. Owners whose lender escrows still receive a copy of the bill, so they can see how the tax was figured.

The City of Murray lists property taxes on its online payments page too. Ask the city whether a bill is open on your parcel before choosing a closing date, and keep every receipt.

  • Request the sheriff's balance for the parcel.
  • Ask the clerk about any older delinquent year.
  • Check with the PVA that an exemption, if you have one, is on the account.
  • Hand the title company the bill number from your stub.

How can I contest a Calloway County value?

Speak with the PVA before anything else, then file with the clerk once the roll closes. Public inspection of the roll lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May, and a conference with the PVA must precede an appeal to the local board, per the state's property tax calendar.

Evidence decides these hearings. Expect the board to weigh land, buildings, rebuild cost and nearby sales. The state's sales comparison approach adjusts neighboring sales for differences like a basement, so collect three or four recent Murray sales and mark where your house differs.

An owner who files but fails to appear cannot take the case further, so attend with your paperwork. After the hearing the board must give a written reason for any increase or decrease, and you are allowed to make an audio recording.

Which exemptions can a Calloway County owner claim?

Owners who live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled, may apply for the homestead exemption. The sheriff's page tells anyone who might qualify to call the PVA at 270-753-3482 rather than pay first.

Only one exemption is allowed per household, and it belongs to the owner instead of the property, so your buyer files a new form. Service-connected totally disabled veterans do not refile each year.

Under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, farm acreage is valued on what it can produce, not on market price. That gap can be wide near town, so anyone selling acres should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

How does the Calloway County housing market compare?

A typical owner-occupied Calloway home is valued at $183,200 for 2020 to 2024, well over Caldwell County's $118,500. Owners live in just 63.9 percent of homes, and renters held 35.8 percent of occupied units in the 2020 count.

Calloway County figures from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page

Household income in the county is $52,706 for 2020 to 2024, and 31.2 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, against 17.1 percent in Caldwell County, a gap that fits a university town. Workers average 17.3 minutes getting to work, the shortest commute of the four counties in this group, so a house close to Murray's jobs and campus has a built-in appeal. The county makes up the Murray micropolitan area, and the 2020 Census put 15,108 households in it.

The county was created in 1822 from Hickman County, and a 1906 fire at the courthouse destroyed almost all of its early records, which is why old title questions sometimes need extra research. Landlords with a rental near campus, heirs with a house in Murray, and owners with a vacant farmhouse can sell as-is to a cash buyer. That route avoids waiting on a buyer's financing and the repair requests that follow an inspection. A signed offer still needs the tax payoff figures above, so collect them before you accept a closing date.

More questions about Calloway County, KY Property Tax Guide

By when must I pay to get the Calloway County discount?

Payments postmarked by November 15 earn the 2% discount, according to the sheriff's page. The dated schedule on the bill is the final word.

Where is the sheriff's tax office in Murray?

701 Olive Street. It serves weekdays until 4:30 p.m., and a drop box on the west side stays open all day and night. The phone is (270) 761-4TAX.

Does the sheriff take credit cards?

Yes, but the sheriff's page says credit cards are accepted only through its website. Cash, check and money order are also accepted, and cash should never go in the mail.

Normally you pay a prorated share at closing and the buyer pays the full bill once issued. The settlement statement shows the split.

Must I fix up a Calloway County house first?

No, a cash buyer can take it as-is. Unpaid property tax is settled from the proceeds, so request payoff amounts from the sheriff and clerk first.

Who to contact in Casey County

  • Casey sheriff official site not found

What makes property tax in Casey County, Kentucky different?

The yearly rhythm matches the rest of Kentucky: the PVA values property as of January 1, the sheriff collects from early October until April 15, and the county clerk picks up what remains. The difference is the setting. Casey County spreads over about 446 square miles with only one city, Liberty, and the 2020 census counted every resident as rural.

That shapes bills in practice. Almost every parcel is a farm tract, a hillside lot in the Knobs or a house on one of the state routes crossing the county, so the assessed value is the first number to examine before you list.

Which Casey County office handles which tax question?

Ask the PVA about value, the sheriff about what you owe this year, and the clerk about anything delinquent. The offices below are the ones the county's own pages list.

Casey County property tax contacts drawn from the PVA site and the clerk's delinquent tax page
OfficeWherePhoneHandles
Property Valuation Administrator133 Courthouse Square, Liberty (mail: P O Box 38)606-787-7621Assessments, homestead applications, appeal conferences
County Clerk625 Campbellsville Street, Liberty (mail: P.O. Box 310)606-787-6471Delinquent tax bills, the annual tax sale, lien releases
SheriffAsk the clerk or PVA for the office addressAsk the clerk or PVA for the current numberCollecting current-year bills

The clerk lists weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, except holidays.

What is the Casey County housing picture?

Small, spread out and mostly owned by the people who live in it. Lincoln County gave up its western portion to form Casey in 1806, and the courthouse in Liberty dates from 1888. The 2020 census recorded 15,941 residents in 6,270 households and 7,366 housing units, 14.9 percent of them vacant. Roughly 76 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied, so many sellers are parting with the home they live in.

Wikipedia describes Casey as the only Kentucky county lying wholly in the Knobs, with its high point at Green River Knob, 1,789 feet. Hillside access, wells, septic systems and road frontage are worth documenting before you list. US 127, KY 80 and KY 49 are among the roads serving the county, and Casey County Schools operates the public schools. The annual Casey County Apple Festival is the county's signature event.

  • Neighbors are Boyle, Lincoln, Pulaski, Russell, Adair, Taylor and Marion counties.
  • Russell and Adair mark a time zone boundary to the south and southwest.
  • With Liberty the lone city, only in-town homes raise city tax questions.

How do Casey County payment dates and penalties work?

The sheriff's bill sets the amount, and the payment date moves the total. KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount for full payment through November 1, the bill amount from November 2 to December 31, a 5 percent penalty during January, and a 10 percent penalty starting February 1, with the sheriff's add-on fee on top.

The lien from an unpaid bill stays on the parcel for eleven years, whoever holds title. If collection starts late in a given year, the Department of Revenue can substitute a schedule that gives owners 30 days at each stage.

Lost the bill? Get the parcel number from the PVA or clerk and ask the sheriff for a copy. Mortgage escrow payments still leave the bill in your name, so confirm the payment posted before closing.

How can I contest a Casey County valuation?

Ask the Casey County PVA for a conference while the tax roll is open to public viewing, a thirteen-day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A phone conference is allowed on request.

When that fails, mail or deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the workday after the viewing period ends, with the parcel, your reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. A hearing follows about a month later. Evidence carries the day: sales of similar houses, construction cost records, an insurance policy or a recent appraisal. Under KRS 133.120 the board denies an appeal if the owner will not hand over reasonable value information when asked.

  • Hold the PVA conference first, because skipping it closes later doors.
  • Keep paying on the value you claimed while the case is pending.
  • A raised value brings a supplemental bill that is due the day it is prepared.

How does the Casey County delinquent tax sale work?

After April 15 an unpaid bill goes to the clerk and can be sold to a private buyer at an annual sale. For the 2025 bills, the Casey County Clerk received the sheriff's list on April 16, 2026, ran the notice in The Casey County News on July 15, 2026, and set the sale for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am in its office on Campbellsville Street. Those dates are behind us, and each year's sale follows a similar summer pattern.

Owners can pay up to the moment the sale opens. Bidders register with the clerk ten days ahead and pay a recording fee of $46 per lien assignment, as the clerk's page lists. Buying more than three certificates in a county, or more than five statewide, also requires registration with the Department of Revenue.

The sale itself runs like a draft. Registered buyers draw numbers at random, then take turns picking certificates from the lists they filed, and for the 2026 sale the clerk planned one certificate per round because of the volume. The clerk's office tells buyers it will not research bills for them, so a parcel with a problem such as a bankruptcy filing is the buyer's risk. Once someone buys your certificate, you owe that buyer and fees can grow. Paying earlier prevents it.

Does Casey County have tax relief for older or disabled owners?

Yes, through the state homestead exemption for owners in their retirement years or with a total disability. A fixed dollar amount comes off the home's assessed value. The Department of Revenue set it at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 and publishes a new amount every second year. File with the Casey County PVA and bring proof such as a driver's license or passport.

The relief belongs to the owner who lives in the house. If you move into care or sell partway through the year, tell the PVA so the next bill reflects it.

How do I close a Casey County sale when tax is unpaid?

Collect written balances from the clerk and the sheriff and hand them to the closing agent. Anything unpaid at the table comes out of your price, and a lien the clerk filed must be released before the buyer takes clean title. Releases are recorded at the clerk's office for a posted fee.

For an inherited, empty or worn-down house, a cash buyer that takes the property as is can pay the tax from the price. That keeps your parcel off the August list, where delinquent bills become public.

More questions about Casey County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where do I find my Casey County property tax bill?

Ask the Casey County sheriff's office, which sends the bills. If you lack its number, the clerk at 606-787-6471 or the PVA at 606-787-7621 can point you to it and help identify your parcel.

When was the 2026 Casey County tax sale?

It was set for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am at the clerk's office, 625 Campbellsville Street in Liberty. Owners could pay their unpaid 2025 bills up to the start of the sale.

How big is the homestead exemption for Casey County owners?

The state figure was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, subtracted from the assessed value. It is open to owners 65 and up or totally disabled, and you apply through the Casey County PVA.

Is it too late to appeal if I missed the May viewing period?

Usually yes. The PVA conference and the clerk filing both fall inside that window, unless the state approved an extension of up to 25 days. Ask the PVA whether one applied.

Does unpaid tax stop me from selling Casey County land?

No. The bill and any lien get cleared at closing from your proceeds. Ask the sheriff or clerk for payoff amounts first so the title company can deduct them.

Christian County by the numbers

What should a Christian County, KY owner know about property tax?

Bills follow Kentucky's statewide calendar, yet the county's scale and its Army connection change how a sale plays out. At 724 square miles it is the second-largest Kentucky county by area and the largest in the west. Hopkinsville is the seat, and the other cities are Crofton, LaFayette, Oak Grove and Pembroke.

Settlers organized the county in 1797. The courthouse in use dates from 1869 and replaced one that Confederate cavalry burned in 1864 because Union troops were using it as barracks. The county runs on Central time and belongs to the Clarksville metropolitan area, with Montgomery and Stewart counties in Tennessee along its southern edge. Hopkins, Muhlenberg, Todd, Trigg and Caldwell counties share the Kentucky borders.

Who do I call in Christian County for each tax or records task?

Most of what a seller needs runs through the county clerk's office at 511 South Main Street in Hopkinsville, whose doors open at 8:00 am and close at 4:00 pm on weekdays. The clerk's own phone menu sorts the common tasks.

Christian County Clerk phone routing for sellers (county website)
What you needNumberNotes
Main clerk line(270) 887-4105Menu extension 3 covers copies of a deed or a plat
Legal records division(270) 887-4109Deeds, mortgages, tax liens and releases filed since 1797
Delinquent tax sale questions(270) 887-4109Number given for the tax sale registration notice
Probate and court records(270) 889-6539Justice Center, not the clerk

For the value of your house, contact the Christian County PVA. For the amount of this year's bill, contact the sheriff's tax office. If you cannot find a current number, ask the clerk's main line to direct you.

How do rentals and Fort Campbell shape the Christian County market?

Half the occupied homes here are rented. The 2020 census counted 26,435 households and 29,206 housing units, with 49.9 percent owner-occupied and 50.1 percent renter-occupied. Median age was 30.0, 9.5 percent of units sat empty, and about 71 percent of people lived in areas the census calls urban.

Many sellers are therefore landlords. A landlord still owes the tax while a tenant lives in the unit, and an unpaid year follows the parcel into any sale. Christian County Public Schools serve most households, while Fort Campbell families are zoned to the federal DoDEA schools. Hopkinsville Community College and regional Murray State campuses are also here. The legal records division of the clerk keeps deeds back to 1797, which helps when a chain of title crosses several generations of owners.

  • Tornadoes crossed northern Christian County in 2006 and 2008 and damaged homes near Crofton.
  • The greatest point of the 2017 eclipse fell near Bainbridge and Sinking Fork, on a farm.
  • Fort Campbell North is a census-designated place inside the county line.

What dates and penalties apply to Christian County bills?

State law fixes them. KRS 134.015 allows a 2 percent discount for full payment through November 1, charges the printed amount through December 31, adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent afterward.

The sheriff's fees ride on top. The Department of Revenue's worked example shows a $1,000 bill reaching $1,254 on the day it moves to the clerk: a $100 penalty, a $110 add-on fee and a $44 commission, using an assumed 4 percent rate. If your house lies inside Hopkinsville, Oak Grove or another city, ask that city whether it bills its own tax and on what dates.

Landlords gain the most from early payment, since 2 percent on several rentals adds up. If a servicer or property manager pays your bill, confirm each year that the payment was made.

How do I dispute a Christian County assessment?

Schedule a conference with the Christian County PVA while the roll is open for public review. The PVA must explain how your number was reached, and a telephone conference is allowed if you ask.

Without a deal, deliver a written appeal to the county clerk the workday after the review period ends. A local board meets about a month later and weighs comparable sales, contracts, insurance policies and, for rentals, income and expense statements. Anyone paid to speak for you must be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, broker, appraiser or your own employee, and must carry your written authority.

  • The board can raise a value as well as lower it, so bring evidence for your number.
  • The state's tax appeals board hears later appeals, though only from owners who first used the county board.
  • Payment on the value you claim stays due while the appeal runs.

When does the Christian County delinquent tax sale happen?

The clerk holds it once a year in summer. The county website set the sale for July 28, 2026, starting at 9:00 am Central, and asked participants to register by close of business on July 20, 2026. Both dates are past, and the next sale will follow a similar schedule.

A state timetable sits behind it. Unpaid bills transfer to the clerk on April 15, and a county sale has to fall between 90 and 135 days after that transfer. In the meantime the county attorney mails notices and the clerk advertises the list at least 30 days ahead. A buyer who wants more than three bills in the county, or more than five statewide, must register with the Department of Revenue 60 days before the sale.

Paying beforehand ends the matter. Paying afterward means dealing with the new lien holder.

Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in Christian County?

Owners aged 65 and up, or totally disabled, living in the home. Revenue lists the deduction at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, taken from the assessed value before tax is figured. Apply at the Christian County PVA with proof of age or disability. Disability claims renew each year, except for veterans with service-connected disabilities and owners with permanent findings from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Ask the PVA how a move, or renting the house out, affects the exemption before you change how the property is used.

How can I sell a Christian County house that owes tax?

Collect payoff figures first and price with them in mind. The sheriff's tax office can state a current balance, and the clerk can say whether an earlier year was filed as a delinquency. The title company subtracts both at closing and records the release.

Moves tied to Fort Campbell can leave little time, and penalties keep running on the statutory dates. A purchaser willing to take the house without repairs can close on your date and clear the tax from your proceeds, which beats catching up in cash while you pack. Ask any buyer to show how the tax payoff and lien release will be handled on the closing statement before you agree to a price.

More questions about Christian County, KY Property Tax Guide

What is the county clerk's address in Christian County, Kentucky?

The clerk is at 511 South Main Street, Hopkinsville, KY 42240, phone (270) 887-4105, on weekdays between 8:00 am and 4:00 pm. The legal records division is at (270) 887-4109.

When was the 2026 Christian County delinquent tax sale?

The county website scheduled it for July 28, 2026 at 9:00 am Central, with registration due July 20, 2026. Both dates are behind us.

What happens to a Christian County tax bill after April 15?

The bill moves from the sheriff to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien attaches to the parcel. Interest of 1 percent a month and clerk and attorney fees are then added.

Do I still owe tax if a renter lives in my Christian County house?

Yes. Property tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, no matter who occupies the house.

Can a Christian County owner past 65 reduce the tax?

Yes, through the homestead exemption, which was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the Christian County PVA and show proof of age.

Which offices value property and collect tax in Graves County, KY?

Two county offices share the work in Graves County, with a third stepping in later. The PVA appraises land and buildings. The county's own PVA page adds that its staff does not set rates and does not take payments. Payments belong at the sheriff's counter, and a bill left unpaid past mid-April is turned over to the County Clerk.

Both the PVA and the Clerk operate from 1102 Paris Road in Mayfield, the PVA in Suite 2 at (270) 247-3301 and the Clerk in Suite 5, where the delinquent real estate tax line is (270) 247-1697. Each office lists its hours as eight to four-thirty. The sheriff keeps the same schedule on Central Time and accepts mailed checks, walk-in payments and online card payments. Cash, check and card are all taken at the counter. The sheriff cannot edit a bill's mailing address, because the PVA keeps that record.

Parcel data can be searched on the qPublic site that the sheriff's tax page recommends for Graves County records.

When do Graves County tax bills go out, and what if one never arrives?

The sheriff starts taking payment on October 1 of the assessment year. If your bill has not turned up by October 10, request a duplicate, which you can collect at the sheriff's office or print from its website.

Bill addresses come from the PVA, not the sheriff. Anything changed after June misses the tax roll for that year, so a seller who moved over the summer may find the bill sitting at the old mailbox.

KRS 134.015 supplies the discount and penalty steps used everywhere in the state. Pay in full by November 1 and keep two percent. The bill sits at face value through the end of the year. January adds five percent, and later payments add ten. The January 1 owner is personally liable for that year's tax, so a buyer who closes in July or October should put the sharing arrangement on paper.

How do I contest a Graves County assessment?

Nothing can be filed until you have talked with the PVA's staff. Kentucky's calendar puts the roll on public display for 13 days beginning in early May.

  • Ask for a PVA conference in or before that display window, and bring questions about how the number was built.
  • Get the appeal form to the Clerk's counter before it closes on the first workday after the display.
  • Assemble comparables, listings, photos of defects, insurance papers and building costs.
  • Make your case to the local appeals board, which sits about a month after the display and explains any change it makes.

Taxpayers may record the hearing on audio. A no-show after filing closes the door on the Kentucky Claims Commission.

What does the homestead exemption save a Graves County owner?

People who have turned 65, and people who are totally disabled, can knock $49,100 off the assessment for 2025-2026. For a house valued at the Census median, $147,800, that leaves $98,700 subject to tax.

The county's PVA page explains that exemptions are never granted on their own. Paperwork goes to the PVA first. Disabled applicants need to have been drawing disability benefits for the entire assessment period, and most must reapply every year.

The deduction follows the resident owner, so a buyer who qualifies files a fresh application.

What happens to a Graves County tax bill after April 15?

At the close of April 15, the sheriff passes every unpaid bill to the County Clerk. The paper becomes a certificate of delinquency, and the Clerk records a lien on the parcel. The sheriff's page states that prior-year taxes cannot be collected there after the transfer.

Notice and sale steps after transfer on a regular schedule (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
StepTiming
First attorney notice mailedWithin a month of transfer
Second notice naming the sale date20 or more days later, and inside 60 days
Published list of delinquent bills30 to 45 days ahead of the sale
Public saleBetween day 90 and day 135

From the day of transfer, one percent a month accrues, and the Clerk and the county attorney each take a commission. Using the state's sample, a $1,000 bill becomes $1,254 at transfer and $1,387.79 when paid inside five business days. After the sale, a third-party certificate holder collects instead of the county.

How should I handle taxes at a Graves County closing?

Say in the contract who pays the current year's bill. Dividing the year between seller and buyer is a private matter, since the sheriff bills only the January 1 owner. Ask the sheriff or Clerk for a payoff ahead of closing.

  • Ask the Clerk's delinquent line whether any earlier year is open, since that lien outlasts the sale.
  • Include the buyer's in-care-of address in the deed, which KRS 382.135 demands.
  • Confirm owner name and acreage on the qPublic record against the deed.

The deed also triggers a transfer tax payable by the seller; the Graves County Clerk page on this site walks through it.

How did the 2021 tornado affect Mayfield and Graves County?

On December 10, 2021, a long-track tornado went through the county and caused widespread damage in Mayfield. The Graves County Courthouse was among the buildings hit hard. Owners rebuilding or clearing a lot should ask the PVA how destroyed or rebuilt structures are valued as of each January 1.

Cash purchasers do buy storm-damaged or half-finished houses as they stand, and the new deed is still filed at the Clerk's office on Paris Road.

What is the Graves County housing market like?

Graves County covers 552 square miles of land at the state's southwestern edge, in the Jackson Purchase, and borders McCracken, Marshall, Calloway, Carlisle and Hickman counties plus two Tennessee counties. It forms the Mayfield micropolitan area, which belongs to the Paducah-Mayfield combined statistical area. It was formed in 1824. Mayfield is the county seat, with Wingo the only other city, and part of the Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge sits inside the lines. Dark-fired tobacco and a woolen mill with clothing makers shaped the early economy, and the county was caught up in the Black Patch Tobacco Wars. Alcohol rules are mixed: the county is limited dry, while Mayfield voters approved store sales in 2016.

  • 37,050 residents in 2025, up 1.1 percent from 2020.
  • 14,139 households and a 76.1 percent ownership rate.
  • Median home value of $147,800, against median gross rent of $775.
  • Median household income of $50,772, with 16.6 percent of residents in poverty.
  • A 56.2 percent labor force participation rate, and 83 new-home permits for 2025.

With so few permits against more than 14,000 households, most sales here are resales, and clear title and condition matter to buyers.

More questions about Graves County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where do Graves County property taxes get paid?

The Graves County Sheriff's Office handles current-year bills by mail, at the counter and online. Once April 15 has passed, the County Clerk handles whatever is open.

What if my Graves County tax bill did not come in the mail?

Request a duplicate from the sheriff if nothing has arrived by October 10. Addresses come from the PVA, and changes made after June are left out of that year's bills.

Does the Graves County homestead exemption apply on its own?

No. A written application to the PVA comes first, at (270) 247-3301, and the $49,100 deduction follows only for owners who have turned 65 or are totally disabled.

When does a Graves County bill move to the County Clerk?

On April 15, at closing time. The Clerk records a lien, the bill is relabeled a certificate of delinquency, and interest starts at one percent monthly.

Can I sell a Graves County house that has unpaid taxes?

Yes. The buyer's title company pays the lien out of the proceeds, so call the Clerk's delinquent line at (270) 247-1697 for the figure.

Who sends a LaRue County property tax bill, and who answers questions about it?

Almost every LaRue County tax office sits inside the courthouse complex on West High Street in Hodgenville, and Hodgenville homeowners get a second bill from City Hall. The sheriff sends and collects the county bill, the PVA sets the value, the clerk takes in bills left unpaid, and the county attorney works on delinquent ones.

Call the PVA before paying when a figure looks off. The sheriff collects whatever amount the bill shows and has no say over value.

What is LaRue County like for a seller?

LaRue County is a rural patch of central Kentucky, 264 square miles of gentle hills just outside the Bluegrass. Hodgenville, the seat, had 3,235 people in 2020 and is where Abraham Lincoln was born. Hardin County gave up its southeastern corner to create LaRue on March 4, 1843, and the Elizabethtown-Fort Knox metro area includes it. Upton, mostly in Hardin County, is the only other city. Buffalo and Magnolia are census-designated places. Kentucky Route 61 runs the 12 miles northwest to Elizabethtown, and U.S. 31E passes through the middle of Hodgenville toward Bardstown and Glasgow.

One school district, LaRue County Schools, serves the whole county, with its campuses in Hodgenville. Lincoln Days fills downtown on the first full weekend of October. LaRue is also a dry county, which matters to anyone trying to sell a building for restaurant use.

How does LaRue County housing compare in the Census survey?

The county grew from 14,867 residents in 2020 to an estimated 15,184 in July 2025, a gain of 2.1 percent. It holds 6,763 housing units. Census survey results for 2020 through 2024 set it apart from the mountain counties to the east:

  • Median home value among owner-occupants: $183,500.
  • Owner share of the 5,996 households: 79.4 percent.
  • Median rent: $860.
  • Median household income: $67,067, with 14.1 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Average commute: 28.2 minutes.
  • Permits for new construction in 2025: 59.

Higher values mean larger tax bills for the same rate, and they make a clean payoff worth the effort before listing.

When do LaRue County bills come due?

The county attorney's office says bills typically mail in October, carry a December 31 due date, and can be paid at the sheriff's desk from November 1 through April 15. Bills for the 2026 year were mailed on October 30, 2026, and the city bills were mailed around the same time. The schedule printed for them follows.

Payment steps for 2026 LaRue County bills (source: local newspaper notice of the sheriff's and city's schedule)
Paid betweenAmount owed
Nov. 1 to Nov. 30, 20262% discount off the bill
Dec. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026Exactly the bill amount
Jan. 1 to Jan. 31, 2027Bill amount with 5% added
Feb. 1, 2027 onwardBill amount with 10% added, plus a possible 11% sheriff's fee on county bills

A card payment online adds a 2.5 percent fee. Inside the courthouse foyer, a drop box takes payments at any hour. By mail, enclose the bill or its number, plus a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt. These steps are reset each year, so check the bill itself.

Is there a separate Hodgenville city tax bill?

Yes. A parcel inside the city gets a county bill from the sheriff and a city bill from City Hall, and the two are paid in different places. City payments go to City Hall, the city website or the city drop box, and the same November 30 cutoff earns the 2 percent discount. A parcel outside the city limits gets only the county bill.

When you buy or sell in Hodgenville, ask the closing agent to confirm that both bills are paid or prorated. The sheriff's page also carries a fire dues waiver form, and the online portal cannot remove fire dues, so an owner seeking a waiver files it at the sheriff's office.

What if my LaRue County assessment is too high?

Ask the PVA, at (270) 358-4202, for a conference. Kentucky requires one before any appeal. The valuation date is January 1, and the tax roll opens for inspection in early May. After that conference the appeal goes to the county clerk right after the inspection period ends, and a board of local property owners hears it within weeks.

The board denies a case that arrives without evidence, so assemble recent sales of similar homes, an appraisal, repair bids or insurance values. The county attorney's office helps the PVA with assessment appeals, according to its page on the county site.

What happens to an unpaid LaRue County bill?

A bill still open on April 15 passes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, which is a lien on the real estate under KRS 134.122. Whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year also owes the bill personally. Penalties and fees are added, and interest at 12 percent a year under KRS 134.125 makes the total rise every month.

  • The county attorney mails two notices before any certificate is sold.
  • After 90 days, KRS 134.452 lets outside buyers purchase it by paying the amount due.
  • The first batch of certificates is usually offered at a tax bill sale in August.
  • An unsold certificate is paid at the clerk's office, Suite 3, 209 W. High Street.
  • A certificate that has been sold must be paid to the buyer.

A certificate cannot be sold while a payment agreement with the county attorney is in place or while the parcel is tied up in foreclosure or bankruptcy litigation that includes that office. The county attorney arranges payment plans on unsold certificates at (270) 358-9223.

Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in LaRue County?

The state set the deduction at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. It is available to owners who have reached 65 or who are totally disabled under a retirement system, for a home they own and occupy on January 1. Apply to the PVA, (270) 358-4202, by the end of December.

The deduction lowers assessed value, so the savings depend on the combined county, school, city and district rates on your parcel. Heirs who take over a house should ask the PVA what changes once the title moves.

Who pays what in LaRue County when a house changes hands?

The January 1 owner is the person on that year's bill, so a spring closing still leaves the seller named. The settlement statement usually divides the year, and the closing agent pays the sheriff. The deed must carry an in-care-of address for the transfer-year bill under KRS 382.135(1)(d), which means giving the buyer's mailing address.

Before listing a LaRue County house with back taxes, collect two numbers: the current-year amount from the sheriff and any delinquent certificate balance from the clerk. Houses that were inherited, behind on payments or too worn for a standard listing can often close faster in a direct cash sale, and the payoffs come out of that one closing as long as they were requested ahead of time.

More questions about Larue County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who takes LaRue County property tax payments?

The sheriff's office at 209 West High Street, Suite 6, by mail, online or in the courthouse drop box. Hodgenville city bills go to City Hall at 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.

Until when did the 2026 LaRue County discount last?

Payments made through November 30, 2026 earned a 2% discount. December 1 through 31 required the face amount, January 2027 added 5%, and after that the penalty is 10%.

How fast does a late LaRue County bill grow?

After April 15 it becomes a certificate of delinquency that earns 12 percent interest a year, plus penalties and fees. The county attorney can discuss a plan if the certificate is unsold.

Where do I sign up for the LaRue County homestead exemption?

At the PVA, (270) 358-4202, before December 31. Qualifying owners are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a retirement system, and must own and occupy the home on January 1.

May I sell a LaRue County house while taxes are overdue?

Yes. The lien stays on the parcel, so the payoff is deducted at closing. Get written amounts from the sheriff and the clerk before picking a date.

Which Lebanon offices share the building at 223 North Spalding Avenue?

Lebanon's county government offices for taxes sit under one address, 223 North Spalding Avenue, so a Marion County owner can finish most paperwork in a single trip. Suite numbers tell you where to go.

  • Sheriff's Office, Suite 101 (270-692-3051): bills and payments, open Monday to Friday between 8:30 and 4:30.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, Suite 202 (270-692-3401): value, name and address changes, and exemption applications, with the same Monday to Friday hours.
  • County Clerk, Suite 102 (270-692-2651): deed recording and delinquent bills. The clerk's own site lists 8:20 to 4:20 on weekdays and a Saturday morning session.

On its FAQ page the sheriff passes valuation and bill-calculation questions to the PVA and sends anyone asking about delinquent bills, or about buying a lien, to the clerk.

What sets Marion County apart from other central Kentucky counties?

Thin settlement defines Marion County: about 57 residents per square mile across 343 square miles of land. Lawmakers formed it in 1834 out of Washington County and gave it the name of Francis Marion. Washington, Boyle, Casey, Taylor, LaRue and Nelson counties surround it.

Three cities exist here. Lebanon, the seat, is the largest, followed by Loretto and Bradfordsville. Gravel Switch, Nerinx, Raywick and St. Mary are smaller places. Wikipedia notes that planar maps put the state's geographic center about three miles north-northwest of Lebanon near KY 429, though neighboring counties dispute it.

Growth has been slow for a century. The first census after formation, in 1840, counted 11,032 residents; later counts ran 16,887 in 1960 and 17,910 in 1980. The tally was 15,499 in 1930, 16,499 in 1990, 18,212 in 2000, 19,820 in 2010 and 19,581 in 2020. By July 2025 the estimate stood at 20,115, a 2.8 percent rise over the 2020 base.

One school district, Marion County Schools, serves every address, with Marion County High School as its comprehensive high school. The Marion County Public Library is in Lebanon. A farm sale has a wrinkle: cropland and pasture are appraised on farm-use value under constitutional Section 172A, while barns and fences are priced at replacement cost minus depreciation.

How do households in Marion County look in the Census data?

Marion County households are settled. More than nine in ten residents were at the same address a year earlier, and owners outnumber renters by more than three to one.

Marion County, Kentucky: figures cited in this guide (Census Bureau QuickFacts)
MeasureValue
Residents, July 2025 estimate20,115

Owners who have paid off their loans spend a median of $415 a month on housing costs. The typical household earns $59,627, and one resident in six lives in poverty. Roughly 87 percent of adults finished high school, while about 15 percent went on to a bachelor's degree. A typical commute runs 22.4 minutes. Veterans total 1,026. The county's 353 employer establishments paid $380.7 million in 2023, and they sit alongside 1,354 firms with no payroll.

Services dominate the economy. In 2022, health care and social assistance took in $110.1 million, lodging and restaurants $25.7 million, and transportation and warehousing $22.0 million, with $230.8 million spent in stores. Residents under 18 make up 22.3 percent of the total, 15.3 percent of people under 65 report a disability, and 86.3 percent of homes have a broadband subscription. Density was 57.8 per square mile in 2010 and 57.1 in 2020, and 57.3 percent of people 16 and older are working or looking for work.

What is the sheriff's collection calendar in Marion County?

Per the sheriff's FAQ, bills are mailed before October 1. Anyone still empty-handed on October 10 should phone for a copy.

  • Oct. 1 to Nov. 1: take two percent off.
  • Nov. 2 to Dec. 31: pay the printed amount.
  • All of January: five percent is added.
  • Feb. 1 to Apr. 15: twenty-one percent is added.

On April 16 whatever remains unpaid shifts to the County Clerk. The twenty-one percent adds the ten percent penalty of KRS 134.015 to the sheriff's collection add-on.

A mailed check should carry the bill number, and a stamped return envelope gets you a receipt. Cards work only at the counter, and the card company's charge falls on the cardholder. The system will not track a partial payment, so send the whole amount at once.

What happens to the bill when a Marion County house sells?

Whoever held the property on January 1 is named on that year's bill. After a sale, the sheriff expects the seller to send the bill on to the buyer, and a buyer left without one can ask the office for a copy. The office adds that it carries no responsibility when a bill is missed during a closing.

Mortgage servicers are not sent a copy. The homeowner receives every bill and must hand it to the lender on time.

For earlier years, call the clerk at 270-692-2651. Overdue bills are transferred there, and the clerk's site advertises a free Online Deed Room. Under KRS 134.420 a tax lien can sit against the land for eleven years, and a title company will want it paid out of the seller's proceeds.

How does a Marion County owner argue with the PVA's number?

Phone 270-692-3401 and request a sit-down. State law makes that meeting the first rung of any appeal, and KRS 133.120 then sends an unresolved case to the clerk as a written petition and on to a hearing. KRS 133.030 opens that hearing between 25 and 35 days after inspection wraps up.

State guidance has PVA staff inspect each Marion County parcel in person every four years or sooner, so find out when yours was visited. Appraisals and nearby sales carry weight. Payment stays due on the amount you claim.

What does the homestead exemption do for a Marion County tax bill?

It removes $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Applied to the county's median home value of $168,100, the taxable base becomes $119,000. The PVA takes applications from owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who live in the house. Since 19.5 percent of Marion County residents are 65 or older, the exemption reaches a sizable share of owners. It stays with the owner, so a buyer applies separately.

What happens at the Marion County Clerk's counter when I record a deed?

The clerk first collects the grantor's transfer tax, which KRS 142.050 sets at fifty cents for every $500 of value or part of $500. A $168,100 sale produces a charge of $168.50. Taxes paid at the clerk's counter can use cash, check, debit or credit card, and the clerk's site warns that cards carry extra fees. Foreclosure sales, divorce transfers between spouses and parent-to-child deeds for nominal value are exempt.

More questions about Marion County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where is the Marion County Sheriff's tax office?

It is at 223 North Spalding Avenue, Suite 101, in Lebanon, phone 270-692-3051. Mailed payments should show the bill number.

How much extra does a Marion County bill cost in February?

The sheriff lists a 21 percent penalty from February 1 to April 15, after 5 percent in January. Bills still open on April 16 go to the clerk.

Does the Marion County sheriff accept partial tax payments?

The sheriff's FAQ says its system does not track partial payments, so send the full bill in one payment.

Which office handles Marion County exemptions?

The PVA, at 270-692-3401. The sheriff refers homestead and disability questions there.

Where do I look up a Marion County delinquent bill?

Call the County Clerk at 270-692-2651. Delinquent bills are transferred to that office, and the clerk's site runs a free Online Deed Room.

Who to contact in Pendleton County

What we confirmed on official pages

Steele (per directory; may have changed), 233 Main Street Courthouse, Room 2, Falmouth, KY 41040; office (859) 654-6055, fax (859) 654-2999; website www.pendletonpva.com; hours 8:00-4:00 Mon-Fri and 8:30-12:00 2nd and last Saturday of month (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Sheriff normally receives tax bills from the County Clerk at end of September and by statute may not accept payment before then; bills usually arrive first week of October; bill shows five due dates/amounts; office recognizes postmarks as evidence of timely payment

Which Falmouth offices deal with tax on a Pendleton County house?

A sale touches three offices in Falmouth. Bills come from the sheriff, values come from the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), and the deed goes to the county clerk, who also takes over any bill that turns delinquent. Pendleton County's website links out to the PVA's own page for parcel lookups and exemption forms.

  • Sheriff: 202 Chapel Street, with tax calls taken at 859-654-4511.
  • County Clerk: Room 1 at 233 Main Street, box 112, Falmouth 41040, telephone 859-654-3380. Weekday service runs 8:30 to 4:00. Saturday service falls on the second and last Saturday of a month, 8:30 until noon, except around holidays.
  • Planning and Zoning: answers for Falmouth and the unincorporated county on floodplains, addresses, code enforcement and plan review.

Statements go to the owner only. Lenders are left off the mailing, so an escrow customer should ask the servicer whether it has a copy.

What dates and amounts apply to the 2026 Pendleton tax bill?

The 2026 statements were mailed on September 30, 2026, in plain envelopes that carry blue lettering reading "2026 Pendleton County Tax Statement." The sheriff asks owners still waiting on October 12 to call. Payment is taken in cash, by check, or on a debit or credit card, though cards add a convenience fee and American Express is refused.

Pendleton County Sheriff schedule for 2026 taxes, applied to a sample $1,000 bill
Payment madeSheriff's posted ruleSample $1,000 bill
During October, through November 1, 20262% discount$980
November 2 until the year endsFace amount$1,000
All of January 20275% penalty$1,050

The third column applies the sheriff's percentages to a round number. Counter service stops on county and state holidays and the weekends beside them, such as Veterans Day, Thanksgiving week, Christmas week, New Year's, Martin Luther King Day and the afternoon of Good Friday. The front door has a drop box under video watch. A check left there should include the stub cut from the top of the bill and a phone number, and a stamped return envelope brings back a receipt. Never put cash in it.

How do appeals and the homestead exemption work in Pendleton County?

Disputes start with a visit to the PVA or a deputy. After that, the owner files at the clerk's office by the workday following the end of public roll inspection, which begins the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. At the hearing, paper wins: insurance policies, construction costs and comparable listings.

Homeowners aged 65 or older, and those classed as totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption. It removes $49,100 from assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. On a house at the county's $159,800 Census median, $110,700 stays taxable. Applications go to the PVA.

What happens to unpaid Pendleton County tax when the house sells?

Delinquent tax is a lien that outlasts a sale, with KRS 134.015(5) allowing up to eleven years. The title search at closing finds it, and the payoff is subtracted from what the seller receives.

When April 15 passes, the sheriff hands the bill to the clerk, interest starts at one percent for each month, and Revenue adds a 10 percent clerk charge and a 20 percent attorney charge. The clerk's site links to a list of advertised delinquent bills. A seller who has fallen behind should ask the clerk for a written payoff before agreeing to a contract. If an outside investor buys the certificate first, the debt is owed to that investor with more fees attached.

What will the seller pay the Pendleton County Clerk at closing?

Kentucky charges the grantor fifty cents for every $500 of declared value (KRS 142.050), and the clerk collects before recording. At the county's $159,800 median value the figure rounds to 320 units, so the tax is $160.00.

  • A deed is $50.00 to record, with $3.00 more per page beyond five.
  • A mortgage is $80.00, and releasing one is $46.00.
  • A deed needs a sworn consideration statement from both parties, plus an address where the next tax bill can be sent (KRS 382.135).
  • Spousal transfers and foreclosure deeds are among the exemptions.

The clerk's schedule says prices vary slightly, so call 859-654-3380 for an exact total before the closing date. Before the day arrives, ask the sheriff on Chapel Street whether the current-year bill is paid, and ask the clerk whether any delinquent certificate sits against the parcel. Bring the tax statement itself to the title company so the proration can be figured from the actual amount.

What is Pendleton County's history and geography?

Pendleton County was formed in 1798 out of Campbell and Bracken counties and took its name from Edmund Pendleton, a Virginia jurist. Falmouth started around 1776 as a hamlet called Forks of Licking, won a charter in 1793 and saw one of the state's earliest sawmills that year. Its courthouse was built in 1848. The railroad created Butler about 1852, and the town incorporated in 1868. During the Civil War, Falmouth hosted a Union recruiting camp from September 1861.

The county measures about 280 square miles, with the Ohio River forming part of its northeastern boundary. Falmouth sits where the Main and South Licking rivers meet, and Butler is ten miles north along the Licking. Kincaid Lake State Park offers 850 acres of camping, golf and swimming. Because the planning office handles floodplain rules, a house near the Licking should have its flood zone confirmed before listing. The school list includes Pendleton County High School, Sharp Middle School, Northern Elementary in Butler and Southern Elementary in Falmouth. The county library at 801 Robbins Avenue offers public computers and a bookable meeting room, and the Fryer House, an 1811 stone home, belongs to the Pendleton County Historical Society. Annual events include the Kentucky Wool Festival, and the Griffin Center Amphitheater and Kincaid Regional Theatre host performances. Falmouth native Phillip Allen Sharp won the 1993 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, and the middle school bears his name.

What does the Census say about housing in Pendleton County?

QuickFacts lists these figures for Pendleton County:

  • 14,800 residents in July 2025, up about 1.1% from the April 2020 base.
  • 6,341 housing units, with owners living in 74.7% of homes.
  • A median owner-occupied value of $159,800 and median gross rent of $793.
  • Monthly owner costs of $1,172 with a mortgage and $475 without one.
  • Median household income of $64,669 and a mean commute of 36.4 minutes.

The 2020 count found 5,533 households and 6,263 housing units, 11.7% of them vacant. About a quarter of households, 24.7%, were one person living alone, and every resident was counted as rural. The Census Bureau recorded zero building permits for 2025, and county population has hovered near 14,000 to 15,000 since 2000. The 2020 census put the median age at 41.6, and QuickFacts shows 19.9% of residents aged 65 or older in 2025, which matters because the homestead exemption starts at 65.

More questions about Pendleton County, KY Property Tax Guide

When did Pendleton County mail its 2026 tax bills?

September 30, 2026. The sheriff asks owners without a statement by October 12 to call 859-654-4511.

How large is the late charge after January in Pendleton County?

It is 21% from February 1 to April 15, 2027. Bills settled in January 2027 take a 5% penalty.

Where is a deed recorded in Pendleton County?

At the County Clerk's office in Room 1 at 233 Main Street, Falmouth. Hours are weekdays 8:30 to 4:00, plus 8:30 to noon on the second and last Saturday.

Who bears the Kentucky transfer tax on a Pendleton County sale?

The seller, as grantor. A sale valued at the $159,800 Census median owes $160.00.

Is a PVA conference required before a Pendleton County appeal?

Yes. The owner meets the PVA or a deputy first, then files with the clerk by the workday after the inspection period closes.

Pike County by the numbers

Where do Pike County property tax payments go?

The sheriff's Tax Division, on Main Street in Pikeville (number 146, Suite 204), takes payment of Pike County taxes. The main number is 606-432-6260 and the tax line is 606-432-6212. Mail goes to the Pike County Sheriff's Office, Tax Division, P.O. Box 839, Pikeville, KY 41502, with checks made out to "Pike County Sheriff."

Ways to pay the Pike County Sheriff, as posted on the sheriff's "Pay Your Taxes" page
Payment typeWhere it is accepted
