The 2026 discount window closed on November 1, 2026, and the face amount applies through December 31. The sheriff's example makes the stakes plain: a $1,000 bill costs $980 inside the discount window, $1,000 afterward, and $1,210 by February.

  • Counter payments are cash, a check payable to the Fleming County Sheriff, or a money order.
  • Cards work at the counter or by phone and add a 2.5 percent service charge.
  • Mail must carry a postmark on or before the deadline.
  • A drop box at the sheriff's door stays open at all hours and is emptied at 8 each morning under camera watch.

How does a Fleming County owner dispute an assessment?

Start with the PVA, because the board will not hear anyone who skipped that step. Kentucky opens the tax roll for inspection for thirteen days beginning the first Monday of May. A conference during that stretch keeps the right to file with the county clerk alive until the next business day after the stretch ends. The Department of Revenue's illustration: inspection from May 3 to May 17 means the clerk must have the paper by the close of May 18.

After that, the local board of assessment appeals convenes 25 to 35 days later. Bring paper. The board turns down any appeal lacking insurance policies, building costs, sale listings or similar proof.

  • At the conference the PVA must walk you through how the value was reached and record the result.
  • A paid agent must hold one of the credentials the state lists, such as attorney, CPA or licensed appraiser, and show your signed authorization.
  • Hearings may be audio-recorded by the taxpayer.

The sheriff will redirect any value complaint to the PVA. Filing and then missing the hearing closes the door to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Is a homestead exemption worth claiming in Fleming County?

For a qualifying owner it is worth claiming. The state deducts $49,100 from the assessed value of the home on the 2025 and 2026 rolls, and the tax is figured on what remains. Fleming County's typical owner-occupied house is valued at $134,700 by the Census Bureau, which would leave $85,600 taxable.

The PVA takes the form. Owners show their age with a birth certificate, license, passport or comparable record. Total disability must be certified by a federal agency or a retirement system, with benefits paid across the entire year, and most such claims have to be re-filed each year; veterans with service-connected disabilities and people found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from that requirement.

If a lender pays the tax from escrow, the sheriff still expects the owner to confirm that it was paid on time. Check the sheriff's record search after the discount period closes.

What happens with Fleming County taxes when a house sells?

The tax follows ownership, and the sheriff will talk through proration for any buyer or seller who calls with a closing date. Under KRS 134.015 the tax is the owner's own debt from the assessment date, and under KRS 134.420 a lien on an unpaid parcel can stay for 11 years after a sale. A sensible order of events: get the balance from the sheriff before listing, then have the closing agent settle the year's bill.

When the sheriff's office closes on April 15, whatever is unpaid goes to the Fleming County Clerk under KRS 134.122. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, commissions and a lien fee follow, and the county attorney writes the owner twice. The clerk then holds a sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer.

The deed also carries a state transfer tax, which the seller pays. It equals $0.50 per $500 of price, so a sale at the county's median value of $134,700 costs $135.00; the 270th block of $500 is only partly filled but counts in full.

Ask the clerk's office in Flemingsburg for any payoff on a transferred bill, and tell the PVA about a new mailing address after closing.

What is the setting for a Fleming County house sale?

Fleming County was cut from Mason County in 1798 and named for Colonel John Fleming. Flemingsburg is the seat, Ewing is the second city and Elizaville is a census-designated place. The county measures 351 square miles, 349 of them land, and borders Mason, Lewis, Rowan, Bath, Nicholas and Robertson counties. The General Assembly gave it the title Covered Bridge Capital of Kentucky in 1998, and the county's courthouse was replaced in 1830 and again in 1952. The 2020 count classed every resident as rural.

Census QuickFacts adds some numbers sellers can use:

  • 15,787 residents in 2025, up 4.7 percent from 2020.
  • 74.8 percent of housing occupied by its owner, across 5,859 households.
  • Typical home value of $134,700 and typical monthly rent of $715.
  • Household income of $49,307 at the median.
  • A commute of 33.1 minutes on average.
  • No building permits issued in 2025.

Without new construction, nearly every buyer is shopping among older houses, so condition matters. A seller who owes taxes or faces repairs can weigh the cost of fixing up a listing against an as-is cash offer.

More questions about Fleming County, KY Property Tax Guide

When do Fleming County tax bills arrive?

Statements typically go out at the end of September. In 2026 the 2 percent discount period began October 1, and an owner who has no bill by then can call 606-845-4701 and press 1.

What does a late payment cost in Fleming County?

January adds 5 percent. From February 1 to April 15 the total reaches 121 percent of the bill, and anything unpaid after that goes to the county clerk.

Where is the Fleming County Sheriff's tax counter?

201 Court Square in Flemingsburg, open weekdays from 8 until 4:30. A drop box at the entrance takes payments around the clock.

Who changes a Fleming County property value?

Only the PVA can, at 606-845-1401. The sheriff cannot alter an assessment, and a PVA conference has to come before any appeal.

Who gets the Fleming County homestead exemption?

Homeowners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and live in the house. It removes $49,100 from the value on the 2025 and 2026 rolls.

What dates matter for a Jackson County bill?

A late mailing can lead Revenue to set an alternative schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff's collecting ends April 15, after which the Clerk holds whatever is unpaid. If your bill never arrives, phone the Sheriff, because a lost bill does not cancel a penalty.

How can a Jackson County owner dispute a value?

The first move is a conference with the PVA. KRS 133.120 treats it as a required first step, scheduled before or during the inspection period, and a telephone conference is available on request.

Still unsatisfied afterward? Mail or deliver a written petition to the County Clerk, naming your reasons and the parcel and stating what you think fair cash value is. It must arrive one workday after the inspection period closes. Rural owners should plan ahead, since the bill itself comes too late to contest.

A public hearing before the board of assessment appeals comes next. Collect the following beforehand:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

A petition without supporting facts can be denied. During the case, tax stays payable on your claimed value.

How much of a Jackson County house does the homestead exemption cover?

Nearly half. The $49,100 deduction for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, set against the Census middle home value of $111,500, leaves $62,400 to tax. That trims the base by about 44 percent.

Applicants need to be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and live in the house. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shown at the PVA proves age. Disability claims renew yearly, with exceptions for veterans with service-connected disabilities and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The deduction attaches to the owner's own residence. After moving, a seller should tell the PVA and file again for the new address.

Who pays when a Jackson County parcel sells with tax unpaid?

The seller should plan to settle it from proceeds. The tax is a personal debt dating from the assessment date, the lien on the land can last 11 years, and at the April 15 cutoff the Clerk files the bill as a certificate of delinquency.

Revenue's explainer gives the timeline. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, with a second within 60 if needed. KRS 134.128 sets the tax sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the Clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days before it.

Revenue's worked example shows the price of waiting: a $1,000 bill becomes a $1,254 certificate at transfer and costs $1,659.90 if paid after the June advertisement. Those totals assume a commission, so ask the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for the real number.

Where does a Jackson County deed get recorded, and what tax applies?

The County Clerk in McKee handles it. The same office issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and gathers the state transfer tax before taking a deed.

KRS 142.050 bills the grantor 50 cents per $500 of value. At $111,500, the Census middle value, the count is exactly 223 units, so the tax is $111.50. Gifts with nominal value, divorcing spouses and foreclosure transfers are among the exempt cases.

Ask the Clerk for the current recording fee before closing, since the statute sets that amount and lawmakers can change it.

What do household numbers say about Jackson County housing?

Jackson County's middle home value of $111,500 is less than half of Jefferson County's $248,400. The county counted 5,122 households in 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.53 people each, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

  • Monthly owner costs: $1,101 with a mortgage and $355 without.
  • Poverty rate: 22.0 percent.
  • Adults 25 or older with a high school diploma: 75.1 percent, and with a bachelor's degree: 8.8 percent.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 83.1 percent.
  • Veterans: 583.
  • Building permits in 2025: zero.

The Census recorded zero building permits for 2025, so new construction added no supply that year. Sellers here are almost always dealing with an existing house, and the assessment on it traces back to the PVA's January 1 value.

What is the Jackson County landscape like for a seller?

Jackson County sits where the Cumberland Plateau meets the Bluegrass, with ground from about 600 to 1,600 feet above sea level. It was formed in 1858 from parts of Madison, Estill, Owsley, Clay, Laurel and Rockcastle counties. McKee is the seat, and Annville is the largest community.

Karst ground in the north produces caves such as Wind Cave near the Turkey Foot campground, and the Middle Fork of the Rockcastle River rises in the south. Some 56,000 acres, about a quarter of the county, belong to the Daniel Boone National Forest, and the Sheltowee Trace trail has a trailhead in McKee. US 421 runs north toward Berea and Richmond and south toward Manchester. KY 30 links the county to I-75 and the Mountain Parkway. There is no hospital in the county, so residents drive to Berea, Richmond, London or Manchester.

  • 13,325 people lived here in 2025, a 2.8 percent gain on 2020.
  • 345.2 square miles of land, with 37.5 people per square mile.
  • Owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes.
  • $665 median gross rent and $40,000 median household income.
  • A mean commute of 37.7 minutes.

Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs, and the Jackson County Fair and Homecoming runs the weekend before Labor Day. Jackson Energy supplies power, and the Jackson County Water Association serves homes outside McKee.

More questions about Jackson County, KY Property Tax Guide

How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?

Write to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, or call (606) 287-7634. Fax goes to (606) 287-7079.

What is the discount for paying early?

Two percent off, provided the full bill is paid by November 1 as KRS 134.015 allows. Afterward the amount on the bill applies until the year ends.

What does a late payment cost?

The statute adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent after that. A bill unpaid at the April 15 cutoff moves to the Clerk, where monthly interest of 1 percent and commissions begin.

Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?

No. The exemption covers the home the owner lives in, so after closing the seller tells the PVA and files again for the new residence.

Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?

Yes. The County Clerk there files deeds and mortgages and collects the transfer tax of 50 cents per $500. Phone (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.

Who to contact in Lewis County

  • Lewis County Sheriff's Office

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Sheriff collects state, county and school property taxes; bill shows a schedule with 2% discount if received by earliest date; later payment costs more (exact dates not on page)
  • Bills go to owner of record as of January 1; homestead/disability exemption questions go to PVA (606) 796-2622

Where do Lewis County, Kentucky owners go about a property tax bill?

Two offices share one address in Vanceburg. Both sit at 112 Second Street, one in Suite 101 and the other in Suite 102, which makes it easy to settle a question about value and a question about payment in the same trip.

Lewis County tax offices in Vanceburg
OfficeWhat it doesLocationPhone
Property Valuation AdministratorAppraises real property, handles exemptions and address changes112 Second Street, Suite 101606-796-2622
Lewis County SheriffMails and collects the current-year bill for the state, county and school districts112 Second Street, Suite 102606-796-2912
Lewis County ClerkTakes over delinquent bills and hosts the appeal filingVanceburg, the county seatListed on the clerk's website

Some bills also carry charges for fire protection or library districts, which the sheriff collects too. The PVA's office page stresses what it does not do: it writes no laws and sets no rates. Those belong to the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, and the PVA only assigns value. Under state rules the office walks every parcel at least once each four years, and since 1992 it may measure the outside of a building with no one home.

What is Lewis County like beyond the tax office?

Up in Kentucky's northeast, Lewis County follows the Ohio River for more miles than any other county in the state. Across the water are Adams and Scioto counties in Ohio, and Greenup, Carter, Rowan, Fleming and Mason counties fill in the Kentucky side. Elevation climbs from 485 feet to 1,400, and oak cut from its wooded hills once ranked among the nation's best lumber.

Mason County gave up the land on December 2, 1806, and the new county took the name of the explorer Meriwether Lewis. The seat has moved twice: Poplar Flat held it first, Clarksburg from 1809 to 1863, and Vanceburg since. Vanceburg and Concord are the only cities, Garrison is the one census-designated place, and Tollesboro, Kinniconick and Laurel are among the many small communities. The 2020 count placed all residents in rural territory.

One school district serves the county, with four elementaries, in Vanceburg, Garrison, Tollesboro and Laurel, plus a middle school and a high school beside KY 10, the AA Highway. Tollesboro's own high school closed in 1994, a closure that stirred real controversy at the time. The county profile counts 814 jobs in health care and social assistance, 680 in construction and 600 in manufacturing, so lumber is no longer the lead.

  • Mean travel time to work: 38.6 minutes.
  • A typical owned home is worth $96,000, and 79.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.
  • Median rent: $751, and median household income: $46,838.
  • Headcount estimated at 12,901 in mid-2025, off 1.4 percent from the 2020 base.

How does the Lewis County sheriff want the bill paid?

The sheriff's page gives three routes. Mail the stub and a check to 112 Second Street, Suite 102, Vanceburg, KY 41179, pay in person at the office, or pay by debit or credit card over the phone or at the counter. Card payments add a fee tied to the bill's amount. Make checks out to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office, write the property ID from the bill on the check, and never mail cash.

Pay only the single figure in the "If Paid By" box at the bottom right of the bill. The subtotals for each taxing jurisdiction are shown for information, and separate payments for each would only cause confusion. A bounced check draws a $25 charge, and the late-payment tiers keep running while you replace it. If you overpaid, phone the sheriff, who may ask for paperwork before refunding. A single payment can cover several parcels as long as each stub is enclosed.

Statute sets the calendar. The state ladder is simple: a 2 percent reward for settling early in the fall, no adjustment during the last two months of the year, then a 5 percent charge in January and 10 percent beyond that. Your own statement prints the exact dollar figure for each window, so trust it over any summary.

What happens when a Lewis County tax bill goes unpaid past April?

Mid-April is the handoff. Whatever the sheriff has not collected by then goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a lien recorded against the house. After that the debt grows by a percent each month, plus commissions for the clerk and the county attorney.

The state's own illustration starts with a $1,000 bill. Clear it within five business days of the handoff and the total is $1,387.79, with the attorney's cut waived. Let the first attorney letter go out and it becomes $1,611.30. Investors can buy these debts at a clerk's sale, which in a usual year lands somewhere between July 14 and August 28.

One exception to the calendar: a bill covering property missing from the roll, or a value that went up on appeal, is payable the day it is drafted, and another 10 percent attaches after a month of silence.

How can I contest a Lewis County valuation?

Ask the PVA's staff for a face-to-face review first. No appeal is accepted without one, and it has to be held ahead of or during the public viewing period.

Viewing runs thirteen days from the opening Monday of May. Having met with the PVA, you can lodge the appeal at the clerk's office until the following workday ends. State law seats the review panel in the county seat, which puts Lewis County hearings in Vanceburg about four to five weeks after viewing wraps up.

  • The board hears only evidence presented with both you and the PVA present, so plan to attend or send an authorized representative.
  • Useful evidence includes photos, insurance policies, construction costs, an appraisal, and nearby listings or sales.
  • Audio recording is your right. The PVA may record only if it gives you written notice.
  • Skipping the board forfeits any later appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Who qualifies for the Lewis County homestead exemption?

The break is for people who live in the house and are either 65 or older or rated totally disabled. The statewide figure for assessment years 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before any rate is multiplied.

The sheriff's page points applicants to the PVA at 606-796-2622. A household gets one, even when both spouses qualify, and a manufactured house or a mobile home taxed as real estate can serve as the residence. After a sale the buyer files fresh, and the seller tells the PVA that title has moved.

What happens to the tax when a Lewis County house sells?

According to the sheriff, sellers typically cover a share at the closing table that matches their months of ownership, and the buyer writes the check for the whole bill when it comes. The closing paperwork shows how your deal split it. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow still lets the owner see the bill, and the owner stays legally responsible for it.

The bill is sent to whoever owned the property on January 1, unless a deed filed afterward carries specific tax bill instructions for the current year. Recording the deed also triggers Kentucky's transfer levy under KRS 142.050, half a dollar for each $500 of price, which the clerk collects. Foreclosures, divorce settlements and gifts from parent to child are among the exemptions. If a tax bill is delinquent, expect the title agent to require a payoff from the sheriff or the clerk before funds are released.

More questions about Lewis County, KY Property Tax Guide

Which phone line answers Lewis County tax questions?

Call the sheriff at 606-796-2912 about payment, and the PVA at 606-796-2622 about value or exemptions. Both offices are at 112 Second Street in Vanceburg.

Can I pay my Lewis County tax with a card?

Yes. The sheriff takes debit and credit cards over the phone or at the office and charges a convenience fee based on the bill's size. Checks go to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office with the property ID written on them.

What does a bounced check cost in Lewis County?

The fee is $25, and the late-payment schedule printed on the bill still applies when you send a replacement payment. Pay the amount for the date your funds actually arrive.

Does my mortgage lender handle the Lewis County bill?

Often, but you still receive a copy and remain legally responsible. If you think escrow covers it and you are unsure, ask the lender, and ask the sheriff if the bill is missing.

Who covers the tax when a Lewis County house is sold?

The settlement statement decides, and sellers usually cover a prorated share for the months they owned the house. The buyer pays the full bill when it comes, and unpaid back taxes must be cleared before the title is clean.

Where do McLean County owners go with a tax question?

If the question is about value, go to the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA); if it is about paying, go to the Sheriff. The PVA takes letters at P.O. Box 246, Calhoun, KY 42327, and answers calls at (270) 273-3291. The Sheriff's Office occupies 135 East 2nd Street in Calhoun, and the Sheriff's page on the county website carries a link to online property tax records.

They run as separate counters. January 1 values and exemption forms belong to the PVA, which cannot accept a payment. The Sheriff accepts money through April 15 and then passes what is left to the County Clerk. A house in Calhoun, Livermore, Island, Sacramento or open country answers to the same two.

How fast do penalties grow on a McLean County bill?

The ladder comes from KRS 134.015. Paying everything by November 1 saves 2 percent, and 2026's date is behind us. From there:

  • The rest of the year: the printed amount.
  • January: 5 percent extra.
  • After January: 10 percent extra.
  • April 15 ends the Sheriff's role, and open bills move to the County Clerk.

If mailing runs late, the state revenue department may switch to a slower schedule of one month each at discount, face value and the 5 percent penalty. Under either schedule the unpaid tax is the taxpayer's own debt, backdated to the assessment date.

What might a McLean County owner expect to pay?

Multiply the Census median of $148,500 by 10.6 cents per $100, the 2025 state rate, and the state's piece is about $157.41. The fiscal court, the school district and other taxing bodies add rates of their own, so ask the PVA for a total on any given address.

The county has been losing people for a century, which limits how many buyers are around. Wikipedia lists the census counts:

Census QuickFacts estimates 9,064 people in 2025 and counts 3,641 households. Owners live in 82.8 percent of the homes, rent runs $641 at the median, and two building permits in 2025 mean a sale is nearly always an existing house.

Can McLean County owners claim a homestead exemption?

Yes, as in every county. A deduction of $49,100 from assessed value covers 2025 and 2026 for anyone 65 or older and anyone found totally disabled. With 22.5 percent of residents at 65 or older, plenty of households fit.

Run the median house through it and $99,400 stays taxable, so the state's slice is about $105.36. The PVA takes the application along with a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. Disability claims need a government or pension finding and a yearly renewal, apart from service-connected veterans and people already ruled permanent and total by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems. Once the house sells, tell the PVA so the deduction leaves the old address.

How does a McLean County owner challenge a valuation?

Book a meeting with the PVA first, since the board of assessment appeals takes only owners who had one.

  • The roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May, with dates advertised in the county's largest newspaper.
  • In the meeting, the PVA explains your number and a form records what was said.
  • Deliver the appeal to the County Clerk before closing time on the business day after inspection ends.
  • Bring paper: land and building descriptions, insurance records, construction costs, and listings or sales of similar property. Bare claims are rejected.

The board sits about a month later and owes you written reasons for any change. Paid representatives must come from the state's list of professions and show your written authority. Skip the hearing and the Kentucky Claims Commission is off the table.

What happens to McLean County taxes still owed at closing?

A lien follows the parcel and does not care who sells it. The County Clerk holds bills still open after April 15 as certificates of delinquency, records the lien, and begins charging 1 percent a month. Under KRS 134.420 the lien survives 11 years, whoever owns the house next.

Costs stack in layers: 10 percent for the Clerk, 20 percent for the county attorney once notices go out, plus postage, advertising and lien fees. The revenue department's own example turns a $1,000 bill into a $1,254 certificate before any of those. Ask the Sheriff for a payoff until April 15 and the Clerk afterward. A certificate can be auctioned 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the buyer may add charges.

What is McLean County like for someone selling a home?

McLean County was carved out on February 6, 1854, from parts of Daviess, Ohio and Muhlenberg counties. Its 256 square miles lie in the Western Coal Fields, inside the Owensboro metropolitan area. The Green River crosses the county from southeast to northwest, with bridges at Calhoun and Livermore and a Corps of Engineers lock and dam, No. 2, at Calhoun. McLean is a dry county where alcohol sales are prohibited.

Calhoun is the seat and Livermore the largest community; Island and Sacramento are also cities. A single county-wide school district runs the high school and middle school, both east of Calhoun on Highway 136, and elementaries in Calhoun, Livermore and Sacramento. Schools at Beech Grove and Island closed long ago. The county is served by a weekly paper, the McLean County News, and sits in the Owensboro radio market. Clocks follow Central time.

Commutes average 31.4 minutes, median household income is $65,596, and 15.8 percent of people live in poverty. Six counties border McLean: Henderson, Daviess, Ohio, Muhlenberg, Hopkins and Webster. A high school diploma is held by 91.7 percent of adults 25 and over, and 85.3 percent of households have broadband for looking up a bill or exemption form. Anyone with an inherited house, a rural parcel or tax still owing can sell for cash as-is. Collect the payoff from the Sheriff and the parcel record from the PVA before naming a price.

The local economy is small. Census business data list 161 employer establishments with 947 employees and a $40 million payroll in 2023, and retail sales of about $92.5 million in 2022. Employment fell 2.7 percent between 2022 and 2023. Wikipedia estimates that 350 to 400 residents are enrolled in some form of higher education at any moment, and the Census counts 430 veterans in the county. With the mean commute at 31.4 minutes, many working residents likely travel outside the county, and the Owensboro metropolitan area is the nearest large job base. Ask the Sheriff, the PVA and the County Clerk each for their piece of the paper trail before you set a closing date, since each office holds a different record on the same parcel.

More questions about McLean County, KY Property Tax Guide

Does the McLean County PVA take payments?

No. Call the PVA at (270) 273-3291 about assessments and exemptions, and pay the Sheriff.

When does a McLean County bill turn delinquent?

The 10 percent penalty starts when January ends. After April 15 the County Clerk gets any open bill, adds a lien and begins monthly interest of 1 percent.

What is the McLean County homestead exemption worth?

It cuts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. People 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply with the PVA in Calhoun.

What would the state collect on a median McLean County home?

Around $157.41 on the $148,500 Census median, using the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100. Other levies are separate.

Who decides a McLean County assessment appeal?

A local board made up of area property owners. It meets about a month after the roll inspection, and you file through the County Clerk once you have seen the PVA.

Where do Perry County property tax questions go?

Hazard holds all three offices a seller needs. Checks to the sheriff are made payable to "Perry County Sheriff." A separate billing provider handles online payment and adds its own convenience fee.

What is the Perry County tax calendar?

The statewide schedule applies. Taxes fall due by the end of December, a 2% discount rewards payment in full by November 1, and January payments take a 5% penalty. Anything paid after January 31 carries 10% under KRS 134.015. Business on April 15 closes the sheriff's collection year. The mailing date changes yearly, so the tax office at 606-439-4523 is the place to confirm what is printed on a given bill.

The sheriff acts as collector of state, county and district taxes, and the office is paid a commission on what it collects. Late-starting years follow a slower pattern in which each stage lasts a full month.

How do Perry County's delinquent bills compare with the face amount?

Delinquency costs more each month it continues. The table below uses the Department of Revenue's own illustration of a $1,000 bill, and the sheriff's real commission rate would shift the totals a little.

Department of Revenue illustration of a $1,000 bill after it reaches the clerk
Point in the processAmount due

Behind those figures are monthly interest of one percent and added clerk and attorney commissions. The clerk's sale comes 90 to 135 days after transfer. The Perry County Clerk's website points to a delinquent tax application, and the county attorney's office can set up an installment plan on a current delinquency.

Can a Perry County owner contest the value?

Yes, and the route starts at the PVA's office, where the owner sits down with staff before anything is filed. The written appeal then goes to the clerk's desk by the end of the day after the thirteen-day roll inspection closes. A panel of neighbors on the local board decides, usually within five weeks, and it looks for hard evidence such as appraisals, repair bids and nearby sales.

Does the homestead exemption apply in Perry County?

Owners aged 65 and over, along with those classed as totally disabled, can claim $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Applied to Perry's Census median owner-occupied value of $91,800, the taxable amount becomes $42,700. Ask the PVA's office for the form and bring proof of age.

What will a Perry County seller pay to record a deed?

The grantor owes Kentucky's transfer tax, a half dollar for every $500 of price in the deed, counting a partial $500 as whole (KRS 142.050), and the clerk takes it before accepting the instrument. On a $91,800 sale that is $92.00. Perry County Clerk's published minimums are $50 for a deed and $80 for a mortgage, and a deed adds $3 for each page after the fifth.

A title company will expect the current tax bill to be paid or prorated, a clerk's payoff if an earlier year went delinquent, and an in-care-of address on the deed for the next bill. The clerk's office can quote the total for any document, and staff there cannot run a title search, so an attorney or abstractor handles that step. The clerk's office also offers a free DocAlert service that emails owners when a deed or mortgage is filed in their name.

How do Census figures describe Perry County housing?

Home values here are the lowest of the three counties in a Census Bureau comparison.

  • Median owner-occupied value: $91,800, against $159,800 in Pendleton County and $112,000 in Pike County.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 70.4%, with median household income of $42,181.

  • Mean commute of 24.8 minutes, and 47.4% of residents aged 16 and over in the civilian labor force.
  • 88.7% of households with broadband, and 14.8% of adults holding a bachelor's degree.

Perry's population fell 6.7% from the 2020 count of 28,473, and the 1940 census counted 47,828 residents. In 2020 the county had 13,213 housing units, 13.1% of them vacant, and QuickFacts shows 13,425 units in 2025 with zero building permits issued. Median rent is $798. Owner costs run $1,167 with a mortgage and $379 without one, and 24.5% of residents are in poverty.

How does Perry County's setting affect a sale?

Perry County covers about 343 square miles of the Appalachian coalfield and touches seven counties, from Breathitt to the north and Harlan to the south to Clay, Leslie, Owsley, Knott and Letcher. The legislature carved it out of Floyd and Clay counties and gave it, and its seat, the name of naval hero Oliver Hazard Perry. Coal and timber shaped its economy, and the Perry County museum keeps that story. The first post office opened in 1824 on the North Fork of the Kentucky River in a settlement then called Perry Court House. Public transit comes from the LKLP Community Action Partnership, with scheduled service in Hazard and links to Hindman, Hyden and Whitesburg, and the Hazard Herald covers local news.

Hazard Community and Technical College and the Hazard ARH Regional Medical Center lead local employment. Receipts from health care and social services totaled $507.7 million in 2022. Hazard and Buckhorn are incorporated cities, while Combs, Diablock, Jeff and part of Vicco are census-designated places. The county's own list of communities runs from Ary and Bulan to Rowdy, on Troublesome Creek, and Viper and Yerkes. Homes are served by two school systems: Perry County Schools, whose high school is Perry County Central, and Hazard Independent Schools, which cover the city. Buckhorn Lake State Resort Park, river access on the North Fork of the Kentucky River and a Trail Town designation draw outdoor visitors, and the county sits inside the first rural Promise Zone, named January 7, 2014.

Business owners should note that Perry County is a stacked occupational license county. The tax is 1% of wages and net profit, and anyone working inside Hazard city limits pays both the county and the city.

More questions about Perry County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Perry County property tax in person?

At the Sheriff's Office, 124 East Main Street, Hazard, on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Payments by post use box 7309, with checks written to Perry County Sheriff.

How much does the homestead exemption take off a Perry County home?

The deduction is $49,100 against assessed value for 2025 and 2026, which leaves a $91,800 home taxable at $42,700.

What transfer tax applies to a Perry County sale?

The rate is a half dollar for every $500 of the price stated in the deed, and the seller pays it. A sale at $91,800 owes $92.00.

Where do unpaid Perry County bills go after April 15?

They move to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency, with interest at one percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees.

Who decides a Perry County assessment appeal?

A local board of area property owners. The owner must meet the PVA first and file with the clerk by the workday after roll inspection closes.

Who to contact in Trigg County

Which Trigg County offices matter for a property tax bill?

Every tax office sits in Cadiz, the county seat, and the county clerk's website lists the phone numbers for all of them. The clerk's real estate line is (270) 522-6661, and the office at 38 Main Street opens weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm.

  • Sheriff, (270) 522-6014: collects the current year's bills.
  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), (270) 522-3271: assigns values, takes exemption applications and holds the meeting that has to precede any appeal.
  • County clerk, (270) 522-6661: handles recording, marriage licenses and delinquent taxes. Vehicle titles and renewals use (270) 522-0217.
  • County attorney, (270) 522-4733: mails the notices that precede a delinquent tax sale.

The clerk also closes for the Trigg County Ham Festival each October. In 2026 that meant half of Thursday, October 8 and all of Friday, October 9, so plan payoff requests around festival week.

Why does Trigg County property differ from other Kentucky counties?

Water shapes everything here. Trigg covers 481 square miles, 40 of them water (8.3 percent), on the far southwest edge of Kentucky beside Lake Barkley. Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, more than 170,000 acres with about 300 miles of natural shoreline on the peninsula between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley, reaches into the county. Cadiz is known as the Antique Capital of Western Kentucky, and Lake Barkley State Resort Park and Prizer Point Marina pull visitors to the shore.

The legislature formed the county in 1820 from Christian and Caldwell counties and named it for Lt. Col. Stephen Trigg, killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782. Lyon, Caldwell, Christian, Calloway and Marshall counties border it, along with Stewart County, Tennessee. Cerulean (partly in Christian County) is a census-designated place, and Golden Pond is listed as a ghost town. The county remained dry until voters narrowly approved off-premises alcohol sales in 2009.

Lake Barkley State Resort Park is known for a lodge billed as the largest wood-beam structure east of the Mississippi, and Prizer Point rents boats, kayaks and paddleboards and offers cabins and RV sites. The Janice Mason Art Museum occupies a restored downtown post office. Each October the Ham Festival fills Cadiz with food and entertainment.

Population topped 14,500 in 1910, sank to 8,620 by 1970 and was back at 14,061 in 2020. July 2025 is estimated at 14,512.

How many Trigg County homes sit empty or serve as second homes?

Counting units against households tells the story. The county has 7,733 housing units but 6,060 households, and the 2020 census called 23.4 percent of units vacant, the highest share among Spencer, Taylor, Todd and Trigg. Rentals stood empty at a rate of 11.7 percent. A county built around two large lakes can show that pattern, though the Census does not give the reason.

  • Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $207,700, and owners occupy 76.9 percent of units.
  • The usual rent is $803 and household income is $59,857.
  • Seniors make up 24.9 percent of residents, the largest share among the four counties, with a 2020 median age of 46.8.
  • No building permits were reported for 2025.
  • Poverty affects 13.9 percent of residents, and 19.6 percent under 65 have a disability.

With that many older owners, the homestead exemption is worth asking about early.

What does the Trigg County economy look like?

Tourism and services carry the local numbers. The Census Bureau counted 231 employer establishments in 2023 with 2,202 employees, a 7.8 percent jump from 2022, the largest gain of the four counties. In 2022 retail sales were $130.9 million, lodging and restaurants took in $25.1 million and medical and social services $40.0 million. Only 51.1 percent of people over 16 are in the workforce, the thinnest share of the four counties, in line with the older age profile. The average trip to work takes 24.3 minutes.

How do Trigg County tax bills and penalties work?

The regular due date under state law falls at year end. Early payers by November 1 get a 2 percent discount; the printed amount applies through year end; January payments carry 5 percent; anything later carries 10 percent. If the state delays bills, the Department of Revenue can swap in an alternative schedule: two full months to pay after mailing, discount in month one, printed amount in month two, a 5 percent penalty for a month and 10 percent after.

Bills unpaid when the sheriff's period closes on April 15 go to the clerk as certificates of delinquency.

What was the 2026 Trigg County delinquent tax sale schedule?

The clerk runs one delinquent tax sale a year, at the end of July in the year after the taxes were due. The calendar for the 2025 bills, which has already run, shows the order of events.

Trigg County delinquent tax sale for the 2025 bills (source: Trigg County Clerk)
StepDate
List of certificates published in the Cadiz RecordJune 4, 2026
Registration deadline for buyers, close of businessJuly 2, 2026
Tax sale at the clerk's office, 38 Main Street, 9:00 amJuly 17, 2026

The list was also open for viewing at the clerk's office on weekdays and on the clerk's website. Owners could pay at the clerk any time before the sale; money that arrived afterward was returned. Some advertised bills were excluded under KRS 134.504(10)(b). Each year's dates and rules document appear on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

How can a Trigg County owner challenge an assessment?

The PVA's conference comes first, before or during the inspection period, and the roll stays open to view for two weeks in May. An owner who has been through the conference files with the county clerk on the next workday after that window.

The local board then convenes within roughly five weeks and can sit for up to five days. The board expects paper, such as lot and building details, insurance policies, what the house cost to build or comparable listings, and rejects an appeal without it. Separately, the PVA appraises most homes from nearby sales and walks each parcel at least every fourth year. Personal property that is taxable must be listed with the PVA between New Year's Day and May 15, and a later filing is treated as omitted.

Who qualifies for the Trigg County homestead exemption?

A resident owner who is 65, or totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessment for 2025 and 2026, provided the house is owned, lived in and kept up on January 1. Applications go to the Trigg County PVA before December 31. Someone classified as totally disabled by an agency outside Kentucky renews every year. Veterans with a service-connected total disability and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security file once.

How do I settle Trigg County taxes when selling?

Request the current payoff from the sheriff and ask the clerk if a certificate of delinquency exists. Under KRS 134.015 the January 1 owner carries that year's tax as a personal debt, and a delinquency lien can outlast a transfer by up to eleven years. When an investor bought the certificate at the July sale, the payoff goes to that investor.

More questions about Trigg County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who collects current property tax in Trigg County?

The sheriff, at (270) 522-6014. After the April 15 cutoff the county clerk, (270) 522-6661, takes over unpaid bills.

When does the Trigg County clerk hold its delinquent tax sale?

Annually, near the end of July. The 2026 sale ran on July 17, 2026, at 9:00 am, and later dates are posted on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

Can I still pay after my Trigg County bill is advertised?

Yes, up to the sale. The clerk's office at 38 Main Street accepts delinquent payments before that date and returns any that arrive afterward.

What is the Trigg County homestead exemption worth?

$49,100 in assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners can file with the PVA at (270) 522-3271 before the year ends.

Can I sell a Trigg County house that owes back taxes?

Yes. Yes. Closing clears the lien out of your sale money, so collect written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk beforehand.

Which Union County offices touch a property tax bill?

Tax work stays in Morganfield, where the PVA and the sheriff share the 100 West Main Street address. The PVA describes itself as a state office with county jurisdiction, charged with valuing property as of January 1. Rates, the arithmetic and the collecting all belong to others.

  • PVA: PO Box 177, Morganfield, KY 42437. Call (270) 389-1933 between 8:00 and 4:00 on weekdays. Exemption forms go here.
  • Sheriff, the payee: PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437. Phone (270) 389-1303, with the same weekday hours.

The county government site adds a tax roll search, a tax calculator and a rate page under the PVA menu, handy for checking a parcel before you call.

What sets Union County apart for someone selling a house?

Union occupies the state's northwest tip, looking over the Ohio River at the spot where the Wabash flows in. The county was created effective January 15, 1811, and together with Posey County, Indiana and Gallatin County, Illinois it marks the point where three states meet. Low wooded hills break up flat farmland, and the high point, 673 feet, is in the Chalybeate Hills inside the Higginson-Henry Wildlife Management Area. The county belongs to the Western Coal Fields region.

Four cities share the county: Morganfield, the seat and largest, plus Sturgis, Uniontown and Waverly. US 60, KY 56 and KY 109 carry the traffic, and the John T. Myers Locks and Dam, opened in 1977, stands 3.5 miles below Uniontown. Union County Public Schools runs elementary schools in Morganfield, Sturgis and Uniontown, one middle school and Union County High School, and the public library has branches in the same three towns.

Union has been losing people for decades. The 1900 census counted 21,326, and the 2020 count was 13,668. The July 2025 estimate is 12,839.

Union County, Kentucky, Census QuickFacts (2020 to 2024 unless dated)
MeasureValue
Change since April 2020Down 6.1 percent

Since the Census shows zero permits for 2025, buyers are choosing among existing houses and will price in how well each one has been kept. Employer businesses numbered 249 in 2023, with 3,980 jobs and payroll near $228 million, and employment grew 8.2 percent that year. Just over half of adults, 52.5 percent, hold or seek a job.

What does the state rate add up to on a Union County house?

Frankfort's real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on each hundred dollars of assessed value, lower than the 10.9 cents charged in 2024. At the $104,500 median home value that is $110.77. County, school and other districts bring the full bill well above it.

The $49,100 homestead deduction brings the taxable base on that house to $55,400 and the state portion to about $58.72. Here, 21.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 23.1 percent of those younger than 65 live with a disability, so many households may be eligible. Apply at the PVA on West Main. A disability based claim needs yearly renewal. Veterans with service connected disabilities and owners deemed permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems do not have to renew.

What is the Union County payment calendar?

KRS 134.015 sets one schedule for all counties. Union's sheriff takes 2 percent off before November 2, bills the face amount until the year ends, charges 5 percent for January and 10 percent once February arrives, and tacks on a sheriff's fee.

On April 15 the sheriff gives the County Clerk its list of overdue bills and a lien goes on each parcel. According to the clerk's page, the sale of those bills normally falls in September, a year after the tax year, with the date put on the website roughly a month earlier. Anyone who wants to bid registers with the clerk first, and the state also requires registration for a buyer taking more than three certificates in this county, more than five statewide, or putting in more than $10,000.

What does a late Union County bill grow into?

The Department of Revenue shows the growth on a model $1,000 bill. A 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add on and an assumed 4 percent commission lift it to $1,254.00 by the time the clerk receives it. Interest of 1 percent a month then runs, and commissions follow the interest.

  • With the attorney's first letter sent: $1,611.30.
  • If settled in May: $1,627.61.
  • Settled in June, after the newspaper notice: $1,659.90.
  • Bought at the sale by an investor: $1,704.21, not counting the investor's own charges.

Under KRS 134.420 the lien can last eleven years, and a new owner inherits it along with the land. If you owe back taxes, ask the clerk for a payoff number and let the title company send it at closing.

How does a Union County owner dispute an assessment?

Meet with the PVA before filing anything, since the state refuses appeals that skip that conversation. Each May the roll is displayed for thirteen days, beginning with the first Monday. After the meeting, hand the appeal to the clerk before the next day ends once display closes.

Local owners acting as the board of assessment appeals convene 25 to 35 days later, for as many as five days. It denies an appeal that lacks factual support, so collect sale comparisons, repair bids and photos. An owner who neither files nor shows up cannot go further to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Any change comes with a written reason, audio recording is allowed, and a higher final figure means an extra bill.

How are deeds and records handled by the Union County Clerk?

The clerk's office at 100 West Main Street holds recorded land documents going back to 1811, mostly deeds, mortgages, assignments and releases. A deed is lodged where the land lies and must cite how the seller got title (KRS 382.110). KRS 382.135 adds the parties' mailing addresses, the full price, an in care of address for that year's bill and a sworn price certificate.

The clerk offers e-filing so a title company can send documents without mail or courier. Residents searching for personal reasons can use the online index free, five searches a day, and the same books can be viewed in the office at no cost. Commercial researchers pay $65 a month per county through the records vendor.

An owner with a tenant, a probate delay or a house needing work can sell as is for cash instead of waiting for a retail buyer's inspection.

More questions about Union County, KY Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay a Union County property tax bill?

Bring it to the sheriff at 100 West Main Street, Morganfield, or mail it to PO Box 30. Questions go to (270) 389-1303 during weekday hours, 8:00 to 4:00.

Does the Union County PVA send my bill?

No. The PVA only values property and handles exemptions, and the county's page says it leaves rates, tax calculation and collection to others. The sheriff handles billing and payment.

When is the Union County delinquent tax sale?

September, in the year after the tax year, is the usual month. The County Clerk posts the exact date on the county website about a month ahead, at (270) 389-1334 for questions.

Can I look up a Union County parcel online?

Yes. The county government site has a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA pages, plus a rate page, so you can see the owner and assessed value.

How much is a house worth in Union County?

The Census midpoint for 2020 to 2024 is $104,500. That is well below the $172,000 in Trimble County and $258,000 in Warren County.

What does the Webster County PVA decide, and what stays with others?

The Property Valuation Administrator is elected locally and assesses every real and personal parcel inside Webster County at fair market value. The PVA's office does not decide your bill. Two ingredients make it: the assessed value, which the PVA supplies, and the rate, which comes from the fiscal court, city governments, the school board, and taxing districts such as the library board and health board.

Some property is valued in Frankfort, among it public service companies and bank shares, and the PVA's own page lists vehicles with them. The PVA may still change a vehicle's value for high mileage or a licensed body shop's estimate.

The PVA's counter is on the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Phone 270-639-7016, Monday through Friday, 8 to 4. The Sheriff's Office, 270-639-5067, shares the courthouse address, and its website carries a Property Taxes page for bill details.

When is the Webster County bill due?

The usual statewide timetable of KRS 134.015 applies. Pay everything by November 1 for 2 percent off. After that the printed amount stands through December, and surcharges start in January. The Sheriff stays the place to pay until April 15. If bills were mailed late, the Department of Revenue can instead run an alternative schedule, so rely on the dates printed on your own bill.

  • Early: through November 1, minus 2 percent.
  • Standard: the bill as printed from November 2 to year end.
  • Late, stage one: January, plus 5 percent.
  • Late, stage two: February through April 15, plus 10 percent.

After that, any open bill moves to the County Clerk, with a recorded lien and added fees. For a payoff after April 15, call the Clerk's office at 270-639-7006.

How fast does a late Webster County bill grow?

Quickly. Revenue's own example uses a $1,000 face amount. The Webster County Clerk's office handles delinquent real estate taxes under the same process, so the progression below is the one an owner should expect.

A $1,000 bill after it moves to the Clerk (Department of Revenue illustration)
StageTotal due
Transfer from the Sheriff, penalty and add-on included$1,254.00
Paid inside five business days$1,387.79
Paid after the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
Paid in May, two months of interest$1,627.61

The sale falls between 90 and 135 days after the handoff. The purchaser inherits the lien and may add its own charges.

What steps does a Webster County owner take to contest a value?

Talk to the PVA or a deputy before anything else, since the state bars appeals from owners who skip that meeting. The appeal itself is filed at the County Clerk's office by close of business the next workday after inspection ends. The board wants documents: building and land details, insurance, construction costs, comparable listings.

  • The roll is displayed for 13 days beginning on the first Monday of May.
  • The board convenes roughly a month after display ends.
  • Taxpayers may make their own audio recording of the hearing.

A late-printed bill uses the value you claimed, with a supplemental bill following if the board sets a higher one. Paid agents must qualify under state rules and carry written authority.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Webster County?

Claim it at the PVA if you live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement plan. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.

Webster County's Census median value is $112,900, which leaves $63,800 taxable. At the state's 10.6 cents per $100 for 2025, the state's cut falls from about $119.67 to about $67.63, with county, city, school, and district rates on top.

Disability claims need payments for the entire assessment period and a new application each year, unless the owner is a disabled veteran or has a permanent total ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Can I list a Webster County house with taxes behind?

Yes, but the debt does not disappear at the closing table. It belongs to the owner from the assessment date (KRS 134.015), and the lien outlives a sale for up to 11 years (KRS 134.420). Get written payoffs before accepting an offer: the Sheriff for this year, the Clerk for earlier ones.

The Clerk's site includes a delinquent tax lookup beside the land records. Should your certificate have been sold at the sale, the payoff goes to the buyer and includes that buyer's fees, so ask who holds it.

The sales contract normally divides the current year's bill by days of ownership. Make sure the split is written down and appears on the closing statement.

What is Webster County, Kentucky, like for a seller?

Created in 1860 from parts of Henderson, Hopkins, and Union counties, Webster County bears Daniel Webster's name. Dixon holds the courthouse, while Providence is the largest of six cities that also include Clay, Sebree, Slaughters, and Wheatcroft. It sits in the Western Coal Field and is the southernmost county of the Evansville, Indiana and Kentucky area. The county runs on Central time, and Wikipedia notes it was mostly pro-Confederate in the Civil War, with skirmishes and guerrilla fighting. Providence and Sebree voted to allow alcohol sales in 2018, and Clay followed in 2022.

  • 12,929 residents in 2025, a 0.7 percent drop from the 2020 base, spread over 332 square miles of land.
  • 5,772 housing units and 4,923 households of 2.53 people.
  • Owner-occupied homes make up 73.8 percent of the stock, valued at a median $112,900.
  • Half of households earn less than $59,628, and 16.1 percent of residents are in poverty.
  • Workers commute 28.7 minutes on average, longer than in neighboring Washington or Wayne County.

The county's population reached 20,974 in 1910, dropped to 15,555 by 1950, and stood at 13,621 in 2010. Owners pay a median $1,241 monthly with a mortgage and $405 without, and renters a median $783. The county has 202 employer establishments with 1,822 employees, and transportation and warehousing receipts of $51.3 million in 2022 outweigh health care receipts of $19.1 million. Only five building permits were issued in 2025, so houses change hands mostly as resales. Inherited homes, houses needing repairs, and those with tax liens can sell as-is for cash and clear the lien at closing.

The Census profile adds more texture. Residents 65 and older are 20.2 percent of the population and under-18s are 24.4 percent. Hispanic or Latino residents make up 9.0 percent, the foreign-born 4.4 percent, and 6.2 percent speak a language besides English at home. High school graduates make up 86.2 percent of adults 25 and over, and 12.8 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Just over 86 percent stayed in the same house for a year, 92.9 percent of households own a computer, and veterans number 527. Retail sales per person were $6,099 in 2022.

More questions about Webster County, KY Property Tax Guide

What are the Webster County PVA's address and hours?

On the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon. Call 270-639-7016 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

Does the Webster County PVA decide my tax rate?

No. The fiscal court, city governments, school board, and districts such as the library and health boards set rates. The PVA only determines assessed value.

By when must a Webster County appeal reach the County Clerk?

Before closing time on the workday after the 13-day roll inspection ends, and only once you have met with the PVA.

How much does the exemption lower a Webster County assessment?

It removes $49,100 from the assessed value of your own home in 2025 and 2026, if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. The PVA handles the application.

Why does a Webster County bill cost more at the Clerk?

A 10 percent penalty and Sheriff's add-on are included at the handoff, then 1 percent monthly interest and commissions follow. Revenue's example grows $1,000 to $1,254 at transfer and about $1,611 after the first notice.

Where does Ballard County sit, and where did it come from?

Ballard County fills the far western tip of Kentucky where the Ohio River meets the Mississippi, in the Jackson Purchase. The county's own site calls it the ninety-third county formed, established February 15, 1842, from parts of Hickman and McCracken, and says it covers 254 square miles. Wikipedia's Census-based total is 274 square miles, including 27 of water.

The first seat was Blandville. A courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 burned most early records, and Wickliffe took over as seat in 1882. A buyer or heir tracing an old parcel can ask the County Clerk which books survive from before 1880.

Which towns and neighborhoods share the same tax offices?

Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are the four cities, and La Center is the largest. Bandana and Lovelaceville are census-designated places. All of the 2020 population was classed as rural, and a single school system, Ballard County Schools, covers the county. Axe Lake Swamp State Nature Preserve, 458 acres in the Barlow Bottoms, is part of a 3,000-acre wetland complex.

Across the Ohio River lie Pulaski and Alexander counties in Illinois, and across the Mississippi lies Mississippi County, Missouri. McCracken County, with the Paducah area, lies east of Ballard and Carlisle County lies south. Ballard is counted in the Paducah, Kentucky and Illinois metropolitan area.

Every one of these places pays through the same three courthouse-area offices:

  • Sheriff, 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe: bills and payments, (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: assessments and exemptions, (270) 335-3400.
  • County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: appeals and, later, unpaid bills, (270) 335-5168.

Is the Ballard County population rising or falling?

It is falling slowly. The population peaked at 14,378 in 1880, fell 41.6 percent to 8,390 by 1890, stayed between 7,900 and 8,800 from 1950 through 2010. By 2020 the count had slipped 6.3 percent to 7,728, and the 2025 estimate is lower again at 7,594. In 2020 there were 3,228 households. Single-person households made up 29.3 percent, and 14.8 percent were someone 65 or older living alone.

When does a Ballard County bill become late?

KRS 134.015 supplies one schedule for every Kentucky county, and Ballard County follows it unless the state allows a delay. Pay in full by November 1 and 2 percent comes off the bill. After that and through December 31 you pay the figure printed. In January 5 percent is added; after January, 10 percent.

The state revenue agency describes the aftermath. A bill unpaid at the end of the day on April 15 is passed to the County Clerk, which records a lien against the parcel. From then, interest accrues at 1 percent for each month, and clerk and county attorney fees are added. Under a delayed schedule each stage lasts a month, so confirm the dates with the sheriff's office.

How does a Ballard County owner's year run?

The Kentucky property tax year as it applies to a Ballard County parcel (revenue.ky.gov)
Month or windowWhat occurs
January 1Value date for real estate
January 1 to March 1Real property listing window
First Monday in May, 13 daysPublic inspection of the tax roll
Day after inspection endsLast day to file an appeal with the clerk
25 to 35 days laterLocal board hears appeals for up to five days
December 31Bills due without penalty

No new listing is needed when last year's roll described a property fully and correctly and nothing major changed. A buyer's deed price can serve as the listed value for the next January 1.

How does a Ballard County appeal work?

An appeal opens with a PVA conference at 132 North 4th Street; the clerk cannot take a filing otherwise. Then you have until the workday after the roll's inspection period closes to file at the County Clerk. State your own opinion of value on the form, because the bill relies on it if it is printed before a decision.

  • Evidence to bring: descriptions of the land and structures, insurance policies, construction costs, nearby sales listings.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you needs recognized credentials and your written authority.
  • You may audio-record the hearing.
  • A higher value set by the board produces a supplemental bill for the difference.

An owner who never files with the local board, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot take the case to a later stage.

Do older residents in Ballard County get a discount?

Owners 65 and over, or classified as totally disabled, claim Kentucky's homestead exemption through the Ballard County PVA. For 2025 and 2026 it subtracts $49,100 from the assessed value; the amount changes every other year. Plenty of residents might qualify: the 2020 census counted 21.4 percent of residents at 65 or above, with a median age of 44.8, and the 2025 estimate of 7,594 people sits 1.8 percent below the April 2020 base.

An owner who never applied might be paying tax on value the state would exempt. A call to the PVA at (270) 335-3400 settles it.

What does a Ballard County house cost, and who lives in them?

Census survey data for 2020 to 2024 show a middle owner-occupied home value of $145,800 and owners in 76.0 percent of occupied homes. Gross rent at the midpoint was $817 and household income at the midpoint was $66,164. The county had 3,209 households and 3,730 housing units in 2025. The 2020 count put the vacancy rate at 12.4 percent of units and a rental vacancy rate of 12.0 percent.

Employers are few: 155 establishments with 1,617 workers in 2023, up 19.2 percent in a year, paying $87.0 million. Commutes average 26.5 minutes, 15.9 percent of residents live in poverty, and 354 are veterans.

Retail sales were $56.7 million in 2022, about $7,415 per resident, and accommodation and food sales were $3.3 million. Among adults, 93.9 percent finished high school and 18.4 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more. Computers are in 95.0 percent of households and broadband in 87.6 percent, which helps owners who want to research a parcel or an appeal online.

Of 195 employer firms in 2023, 5 were minority-owned, the county has 510 nonemployer businesses, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Households average 2.35 people, 12.3 percent of residents under 65 report a disability, and 6.0 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance. No building-permit total was reported for 2025.

How do taxes work when a Ballard County house is sold?

Kentucky treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien, once recorded, can stay on the land for as long as eleven years whoever owns it. A closing agent therefore tends to pay the year's bill from the seller's proceeds. Ask how that year is divided with the buyer.

  • Sheriff: what is owed this year and in past years.
  • Clerk: whether a lien is on record.
  • Deed: add the next bill's mailing address, which KRS 382.135 requires.

Owners who inherited a river-county house or moved away and now owe back taxes can request a written cash offer. Any lien balance is paid out of the price.

More questions about Ballard County, KY Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay in Ballard County?

Payments go to the Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe. The county's page for elected offices lists (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

How much do I save by paying early?

Two percent of the bill, provided the sheriff has the full amount by November 1 (KRS 134.015). After that date the printed amount stands through December 31.

What if December 31 passes?

The bill picks up 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward. Once April 15 passes, the County Clerk holds it and interest of 1 percent a month runs.

Where is an assessment appeal filed?

File with the County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, after your PVA conference. Filing closes the workday after inspection ends.

Is the homestead exemption a county program?

No, the state runs it. The Ballard County PVA, (270) 335-3400, takes applications from owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and the 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100.

What is Hancock County, Kentucky like for someone selling a house?

Hancock County hugs the Ohio River on Kentucky's northwest side. Hawesville is the seat, Lewisport is the biggest town, and the river separates the county from Spencer and Perry counties in Indiana. The county was carved out in 1829 from slices of Breckinridge, Daviess and Ohio counties and carries the name of John Hancock. Its courthouse dates to 1868 and was renovated in 1978, and the county sits inside the Owensboro metro area.

Industry lines the riverbank. The county industrial foundation describes three aluminum plants and a paper mill, with over 2,000 workers between them, plus smaller manufacturers. Hawesville's 1902 railroad depot, where Harry Truman stopped during his 1948 campaign, is now the county museum and opens on Sundays from April through October. Vastwood Park covers nearly 400 acres on US 60 between Hawesville and Lewisport, with a 19 acre lake and a paved 1.1 mile trail.

The Census Bureau counted 15 building permits for 2025. A Hancock County seller is usually offering a resale house in a small market, where new construction rarely sets the price.

Which offices handle a Hancock County property tax bill?

Three offices share the Hancock County Administration Building at 225 Main Cross Street in Hawesville, and each has a separate job.

  • Sheriff, first floor: takes payment. Phone 270-927-6247, mail to P.O. Box 427. The posted hours are 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.
  • PVA: values property, and has no say over rates or payments. It reads the market each January 1 and aims for what a willing buyer would pay. Phone 270-927-6846, mail to P.O. Box 523.
  • County Clerk, second floor: keeps land records and processes delinquent real estate taxes. Phone 270-927-6117, mail to P.O. Box 146.

The state's Department of Revenue supervises the PVA's work and runs yearly studies in every county to check that assessments meet constitutional standards.

When do Hancock County tax bills fall due?

Bills reach the sheriff by mid September. Until then the PVA mails the current year bill to whatever in care of address appears in the deed. KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount for full payment on or before November 1 and sets face value for the rest of the year.

Miss that and January adds 5 percent. Past January 31 the penalty doubles to 10 percent and the sheriff tacks on another 10 percent, which the state describes as 21 percent combined. When the state delays mailing, an alternative schedule gives 30 days per stage instead. The bill in your hand carries the dates that apply.

Whoever owned the house on January 1 is the taxpayer of record for that year, so a closing in October or November is the moment to ask the sheriff for the exact discount cutoff.

What do the Census Bureau's numbers show for Hancock County?

Homeowners dominate and prices are modest, as the snapshot below shows.

Snapshot of Hancock County from Census Bureau data
MeasureValue
Residents, 2020 count9,095
Residents, July 2025 estimate9,050
Housing units, July 20253,968
Owners as a share of households77.2%
Typical owned home value$141,200
Typical monthly rent$740
Typical household income$65,464
Land area187.67 square miles

About 20.6 percent of residents are past their 65th birthday, so a good share of Hancock County owners are old enough for the homestead exemption described below. With a typical home near $141,200, a few years of missed bills plus penalties can take a visible bite out of a sale price.

Do Hancock County rental owners owe an occupational fee?

Yes. The county's occupational tax page says every person or business with activity in Hancock County pays on net profits, and it names rental property owners, farmers and home based businesses in that group. The rate on business profits has been 1.60 percent since January 1, 2020, and an annual business license costs $10.

Employees working inside the county pay 1.60 percent of gross wages, withheld by the employer. Two exceptions apply: a company employing more than 100 people in manufacturing in the county does not owe the net profits fee, and neither does a business that pays the county a franchise tax.

A landlord selling a Hancock County rental should expect a net profits return for the year of the sale. The Occupational Tax Office, upstairs on the third floor, answers at 270-927-8788.

How can I contest a Hancock County assessment?

Meet the PVA first. Call 270-927-6846 to book a conference in the spring inspection window, which no appeal can skip. If the talk ends without a deal, you have one workday after the window closes to file with the clerk upstairs, along with the value you claim.

The local appeals board, three people, hears the case about five weeks later and expects evidence from you. The Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals hears anything further. Ask the PVA which sales it relied on, then bring your own comparable sales.

Who gets the homestead exemption in Hancock County?

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled, can ask the PVA to lower the taxable value of their own residence. KRS 132.810 allows one exemption per household unit and treats a manufactured house as a unit. After a sale, the old owner reports the transfer and the new owner applies separately. Ask the PVA for the dollar figure in force.

What should a Hancock County seller check before closing?

A short checklist keeps surprises away from the table.

  • Confirm the deed carries a mailing address for the new owner's tax bill, which KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Ask the sheriff whether a current year bill is open and who will pay it, since the bill covers a full calendar year.
  • Search the parcel through the clerk's website, which links a delinquent tax tool (DTax) and eCCLIX, a viewer for filed land records that helps when a house came through an estate.
  • Pull permits for any addition. Planning and Zoning is at 200 Court Square, P.O. Box 692, open Monday, Wednesday and Friday from 8 a.m. to noon at 270-927-8169.

The Hancock County Urban Planning Commission holds evening meetings every other month, starting the first Monday of February.

What happens to an unpaid Hancock County bill?

A bill still open when April 15 ends leaves the sheriff and lands with the clerk as a certificate of delinquency. The clerk's DTax tool shows what the county believes is owed on a parcel, with a warning that the clerk fixes the true figure at payment or sale. Interest, a clerk commission and later an attorney commission pile on, and a buyer of the certificate adds more. A seller who plans to list in summer should pay or collect a written payoff before certificate sales begin in July.

Back taxes do not block a sale. The settlement agent pays the payoff from the proceeds, the same way it works with a cash buyer who purchases as is.

More questions about Hancock County, KY Property Tax Guide

Do rental owners in Hancock County pay occupational tax?

Yes. Rental property owners pay on net profits at 1.60 percent, plus a $10 annual business license. The Occupational Tax Office at 270-927-8788 takes the forms.

When does the Hancock County Urban Planning Commission meet?

Every other month, starting with the first Monday of February. Meetings begin at 7 p.m. on the third floor of the Administration Building, 225 Main Cross Street.

How can I view recorded deeds for a Hancock County house?

Through eCCLIX on the County Clerk's website, which lets you view or print filed documents. Questions go to 270-927-6117.

I bought a Hancock County home and never got a tax bill. Who do I call?

The sheriff at 270-927-6247 can provide a copy. The PVA mails the bill to the address in the deed until preparation begins in mid September, which is why that address matters.

Is the PVA or the sheriff the office that takes the payment?

The sheriff. The PVA's role ends at valuation, and payments go to the Hancock County Sheriff's Office downstairs on the first floor.

Selling in Lyon County? Get a Cash Offer

Who to contact in Lyon County

  • Lyon County Sheriff's Office

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Listed PVA website: www.lyonkypva.com
  • Bills received from County Clerk end of September; sheriff cannot accept payment earlier; no partial payments; postmarks accepted; after April 15 pay at County Clerk (270-388-2331)

Selling in Lyon County?
